Acknowledgments

致谢

It’s funny how a book takes on a life of its own. This one began like most others—first as a compilation of research,

expressed knowledge, and the inspiration and ideas of an author or two. But now after many years have passed and

many thousands of people have read, shared, used, and reflected on the content from its pages, this book has grown

into something much more—something far greater than anything I ever expected. For many, Herbs for Pets has

become a gold standard—the definitive guide to herbs for pets. But it is not the authors, nor even the information

contained in its pages, that stand at the forefront of this book’s resounding success. It’s the growing audiences of pet

loving people who are realizing that the biggest rewards of animal companionship can come only after we learn to

accept and respect the true nature of our animals. Without people like you, this latest edition would not exist. Thank

you.

一本书拥有自己的生命，这很有趣。这篇文章和大多数其他文章一样，首先是研究、表达的知识以及一两

位作者的灵感和想法的汇编。但现在，许多年过去了，成千上万的人阅读、分享、使用和反思了书中的内

容，这本书已经发展得更加丰富——远远超出了我的预期。对于许多人来说，《宠物草药》已成为黄金标

准——宠物草药的权威指南。但这本书取得巨大成功的关键并不是作者，甚至不是书中所包含的信息。越

来越多的爱宠人士意识到，只有在我们学会接受和尊重动物的真实本性之后，动物陪伴才能带来最大的回

报。没有像您这样的人，就不会存在这个最新版本。谢谢。

And once again—thank you to my now ex-wife and forever friend, Mary, who remains one of my foremost

herbalist teachers. Thanks also go to Nancy Kerns, editor of Whole Dog Journal magazine, who throughout the

years has been keeping the “holistic word” alive and visible to so many like-hearted animal lovers. And thanks to

my dear friend Ikuko Kanada, who not only translated this tome into Japanese but also has been at the forefront of a

new natural pet care revolution in Japan; your work brings renewed hope and inspiration to all who truly care about

animal wellness. Thank you to Gail Pope and all of the incredible people at Brighthaven Sanctuary—a place where,

because of you, miracles really do happen.

再次感谢我现在的前妻和永远的朋友玛丽，她仍然是我最重要的草药老师之一。还要感谢《Whole Dog

Journal》杂志的编辑南希·克恩斯 (Nancy Kerns)，多年来，她一直让“整体一词”保持活力，并为许多志同道

合的动物爱好者所熟知。感谢我亲爱的朋友金田育子，她不仅将这本书翻译成日语，而且一直站在日本新

的天然宠物护理革命的最前沿；您的工作为所有真正关心动物健康的人带来了新的希望和灵感。感谢盖尔·

波普 (Gail Pope) 和布莱特黑文庇护所 (Brighthaven Sanctuary) 的所有令人难以置信的人们——因为有你们，

奇迹才真正发生。

A special thanks to all of you who came to our rescue when my home burned in the Montana fires of 2000. There

is absolutely nothing to describe the feelings of love coming from so many people.

特别感谢 2000 年蒙大拿州大火中我的家被烧毁时伸出援手的所有人。绝对没有什么可以形容这么多人的

爱的感觉。

And of course, thank you to all of the wonderful holistic veterinarians and natural pet-care providers who work on

the front lines to bring the gifts of human intellect, love, and compassion to the true innocents of the world: the

animals.

当然，还要感谢所有出色的整体兽医和天然宠物护理人员，他们工作在第一线，将人类的智慧、爱和同

情心的礼物带给世界上真正的无辜者：动物。

—Greg L. Tilford

——格雷格·L·蒂尔福德

Introduction

介绍

Herbs and animals have lived together for a long, long time. Millions of years before the first human walked the

earth, creatures large and small were using plants as their primary source of healing. In fact, much of our modern

medicine originates from what early humans learned through observation of wild animals and their instinctive uses

of plants. For instance, we know that Indian tribes of the western United States learned of the powerful antimicrobial

properties of Ligusticum porteri by observing bears ingest and roll in the plants to heal themselves. Even today, the

plant is still known by many as “bear medicine.”

草药和动物一起生活了很长很长一段时间。在第一个人类出现在地球上的数百万年前，大大小小的生物就

开始使用植物作为主要的治疗来源。事实上，我们的现代医学很大程度上源于早期人类通过观察野生动物

及其对植物的本能使用所学到的知识。例如，我们知道，美国西部的印第安部落通过观察熊摄入并在植物

中打滚来治愈自己，了解了藁本的强大抗菌特性。即使在今天，这种植物仍然被许多人称为“熊药”。

In the face of diseases such as AIDS and cancer, modern-day pharmaceutical researchers continue to scour the

remaining wilds of our planet in search of cures, and once again we are turning to the animals for answers.

Zoopharmacognosy, a new discipline of science that investigates how animals use plants to heal themselves, is

attracting attention at leading research universities throughout the world. At the forefront of the zoopharmacognosy

=== PAGE 11 ===
effort are Dr. Eloy Rodriguez, a biochemist specializing in natural products and synthetic chemistry, and Harvard

primatologist Richard Wrangham, who has been studying chimpanzees and gorillas in their native African habitats.

Rodriguez and Wrangham have discovered that the apes have an innate ability to select specific plant species for use

against internal parasites. In fact, not only can the animals select plants that possess specific medicinal compounds

that are effective at expelling their parasites but somehow they know exactly how much plant material is needed to

initiate a cure without causing toxic side effects.

面对艾滋病和癌症等疾病，现代药物研究人员继续在地球上剩余的荒野中寻找治疗方法，我们再次向动

物寻求答案。动物生药学是一门新的科学学科，研究动物如何利用植物来治愈自己，正在吸引世界各地领

先研究大学的关注。走在动物生药学研究前沿的是 Eloy Rodriguez 博士（专门研究天然产物和合成化学的

生物化学家）和哈佛大学灵长类动物学家 Richard Wrangham（一直在非洲本土栖息地研究黑猩猩和大猩

猩）。罗德里格斯和兰厄姆发现，猿类具有选择特定植物物种来对抗体内寄生虫的先天能力。事实上，动

物不仅可以选择含有能有效驱除寄生虫的特定药用化合物的植物，而且它们还确切地知道需要多少植物材

料来启动治疗而不引起毒副作用。

As zoopharmacognosy recaptures our attention and as our respect toward the healing wisdom of animals grows,

our quest for herbal curative answers is becoming more urgent. But we’re faced with a problem. Strains of bacteria

once thought to be conquered are reemerging despite our antibiotics, and healing resources are disappearing faster

than we can discover them. Tens of thousands of acres of wild lands are lost each day to the effects of a growing

human population and the relentless demands we place upon the planet. The Smithsonian Institution and fifteen

other research organizations recently completed a twenty-year study that concluded that at least one in every eight

plant species worldwide are currently at risk of becoming extinct.

随着动物生药学重新引起我们的注意，随着我们对动物治疗智慧的尊重不断增长，我们对草药治疗答案

的追求变得更加紧迫。但我们面临着一个问题。尽管我们使用了抗生素，曾经被认为已被征服的细菌菌株

却重新出现，而治疗资源的消失速度比我们发现它们的速度还要快。由于人口增长和我们对地球的无情要

求，每天都有数万英亩的荒地消失。史密森学会和其他 15 个研究组织最近完成了一项历时 20 年的研究，

得出的结论是，目前全世界至少有八分之一的植物物种面临灭绝的风险。

In North America alone, it is estimated that 29 percent of sixteen thousand plant species are on the verge of

disappearing forever—and with each loss, a vital connecting link between earth and all the creatures who walk her

=== PAGE 12 ===
ground is being broken forever.

据估计，仅在北美，一万六千种植物中有 29% 正处于永远消失的边缘，而随着每一次消失，地球与所有

行走在其土地上的生物之间的重要联系纽带也将永远断裂。

As scientists struggle to find cures before plants are eliminated from the face of the planet, a tremendous “green

revolution” is under way. A growing number of people are coming to realize that much of the healing wisdom we

seek rests not in science and technology but within the ancient healing traditions of nature itself. To access this

awareness, we find ourselves turning to the aboriginal peoples (who adopted healing ways from observing animals)

to relearn ways of healing that have been passed down through hundreds of generations from humankind’s oldest

teachers—the animals.

当科学家们努力在植物从地球表面消失之前找到治疗方法时，一场巨大的“绿色革命”正在进行。越来越

多的人开始意识到，我们寻求的许多治疗智慧并不在于科学和技术，而在于大自然本身的古老治疗传统。

为了获得这种意识，我们发现自己转向原住民（他们通过观察动物而采用了治疗方法）来重新学习从人类

最古老的老师——动物那里传承了数百代的治疗方法。

Ancient cultures knew that healthful living, healing, and good medicine are not gauged by how effectively people

can exploit the medicinal properties of natural resources. Instead, shamans and medicine women of the past saw

human health as an integral part of the living celestial body we have since grown to know as Earth. They knew that

our gravest ills emanate not from what nature bestows upon us but from what we bestow upon nature. This message

is being repeated to us everywhere in the form of ancient bacteria, once thought to be conquered, that are mutating

into stronger, more resistant, more aggressive strains of infectious disease. Vaccines that we once viewed as miracle

medicines are now thought to debilitate the immune system they were designed to support and protect. Heart

disease, cancer, arthritis, osteoporosis, and even psychosis-driven murder are being linked to the stresses of modern

society and the nutrition-depleted foods we eat. Violent rainstorms of unprecedented ferocity wreak havoc as a by-

product of air pollution and the effects of global warming. You may ask, how is all of this relevant to a book about

herbal animal care? The answer: in the most fundamental ways imaginable.

古代文化知道，健康的生活、治疗和良好的医学并不是通过人们如何有效地利用自然资源的药用特性来

衡量的。相反，过去的萨满和女巫医将人类健康视为生命天体不可分割的一部分，我们后来称之为地球。

他们知道，我们最严重的疾病不是源于自然赋予我们的东西，而是源于我们赋予自然的东西。这一信息正

在以古老细菌的形式向我们各处重复，这些细菌一度被认为已被征服，但它们正在变异为更强大、更具抵

抗力、更具攻击性的传染病菌株。我们曾经视为神奇药物的疫苗现在被认为会削弱它们原本支持和保护的

免疫系统。心脏病、癌症、关节炎、骨质疏松症，甚至精神病驱动的谋杀都与现代社会的压力和我们所吃

的营养匮乏的食物有关。作为空气污染和全球变暖影响的副产品，前所未有的猛烈暴雨造成了严重破坏。

您可能会问，所有这些与一本有关草药动物护理的书有什么关系？答案：以可以想象的最基本的方式。

This book introduces you to hundreds of plant medicines that can be used in the daily care of animals. In the first

chapters, you learn the importance of feeding your companion a natural whole-foods diet. Then step by step you are

guided into new levels of self-reliance as you learn to select, prepare, and apply natural remedies, many of which

may be as accessible as your own backyard, on behalf of your companion animal. To help overcome possible

skepticism, we have provided references to hundreds of cutting-edge scientific studies that support the effectiveness

of herbs in animals. But even more significant to the purposes of this book, we share what herbalists and animals

have learned in the absence of science (without the cruel inhumanities of animal testing) from thousands of years of

continuously safe and effective herb use.

本书向您介绍了数百种可用于动物日常护理的植物药物。在第一章中，您将了解为您的同伴提供天然全

食物饮食的重要性。然后，当您学习选择、准备和应用自然疗法时，您将逐步进入自力更生的新水平，其

中许多可能就像您自己的后院一样，为您的伴侣动物提供帮助。为了帮助克服可能的怀疑，我们提供了数

百项尖端科学研究的参考资料，这些研究支持草药在动物中的有效性。但对本书的目的来说更重要的是，

我们分享了草药师和动物在没有科学的情况下（没有残酷的不人道的动物测试）从数千年来持续安全有效

的草药使用中学到的东西。

However, all of this represents the lesser side of what this book has to offer. Our deepest wish is to pass on the

sense of interconnectedness that grows within the heart of the healer, as he or she learns and accepts ancient ways of

healing that have been utilized by all life-forms on earth. This is not just a book about finding alternatives to

conventional drugs; it is one about honoring and supporting a system of health care and healing that far exceeds the

effectiveness of any medicine devised by humans—a system contained in and shared among the bodies of animals,

=== PAGE 13 ===
plants, and Mother Earth herself.

然而，所有这些都代表了本书所提供的较小的一面。我们最深切的愿望是，当治疗师学习并接受地球上

所有生命形式都使用的古老治疗方法时，将其心中生长的相互联系感传递下去。这不仅仅是一本关于寻找

传统药物替代品的书；它也是一本关于寻找传统药物替代品的书。它是关于尊重和支持远远超过人类设计

的任何药物有效性的医疗保健和治疗系统的一个系统，这个系统包含在动物、植物和地球母亲的身体中并

由它们共享。

In nature, plants represent much more than containers of active chemical constituents that have been identified

and validated by the halls of human science. They are healing delegates of nature’s design, here to serve the needs of

all creatures who benefit from the nectar of their flowers, the shelter of their leaves, and the healing powers they

hold. They are the critical link between what is alive and what is not, providing us and other organisms with the

oxygen that is necessary for life and the base elements of the food chain—from macrobiotic soil nutrients to the

vegetables on our dinner plates. Yet most people see plants as humanity’s gift: insignificant by virtue of their silence

but powerful and valuable when their secrets are revealed by science. Likewise, most of humanity still sees animals

as expendable, lower forms of life that exist without intelligent consciousness or emotional pain and that offer no

resistance when exploited.

在自然界中，植物不仅仅代表人类科学殿堂已识别和验证的活性化学成分的容器。它们是大自然设计的

治愈代表，在这里服务于所有受益于花朵的花蜜、叶子的庇护和它们所拥有的治愈力量的生物的需求。它

们是生命与非生命之间的关键纽带，为我们和其他生物体提供生命所需的氧气和食物链的基本要素——从

长寿土壤养分到我们餐盘上的蔬菜。然而，大多数人将植物视为人类的礼物：由于它们的沉默而微不足

道，但当它们的秘密被科学揭示时，它们就变得强大而有价值。同样，大多数人类仍然将动物视为可消耗

的低等生命形式，它们的存在没有智慧意识或情感痛苦，并且在被剥削时不会提供任何抵抗。

In the minds of millions of people, plants and animals are here for the sole purpose of serving us, as fruits and

beasts of burden without equal rights, in the pursuit of health and happiness. Whether it be a feedlot steer or a

companion German shepherd dog, the needs of most animals become secondary concerns when we are buying pet

food at the grocery store or when a chronic immune system disorder erupts into a household flea infestation. Instead

of addressing their pet’s real needs, many pet owners are predisposed to remain focused on themselves—the grocery

bill dictates the quality of nutrition their animals receive, and fleas are approached as something that invades our

=== PAGE 14 ===
homes, rather than as a symptom of a weakened animal host.

在数百万人的心目中，植物和动物存在的唯一目的是为我们服务，作为没有平等权利的果实和驮兽，追

求健康和幸福。无论是饲养场的公牛还是伴侣德国牧羊犬，当我们在杂货店购买宠物食品或当慢性免疫系

统疾病爆发为家庭跳蚤感染时，大多数动物的需求都成为次要问题。许多宠物主人并没有满足宠物的真正

需求，而是倾向于继续关注自己——食品杂货账单决定了他们的动物所接受的营养质量，而跳蚤被视为入

侵我们家庭的东西，而不是作为身体虚弱的症状。动物宿主。

With Herbs for Pets, we hope to precipitate a change in this paradigm. The fact that you are reading this book

implies that you are not like most people—in fact, you are part of a growing community of special human beings

who are on a healing path that leads to something much more significant than the simple joy derived from opening

up a can of cat food for the cat or giving the family dog rawhides to keep him busy. Like us, the authors of this

通过 Herbs for Pets，我们希望能够推动这种模式的改变。你正在阅读这本书的事实意味着你与大多数人

When we provide our companion animals with considerations of health and healing that meet their needs and not

当我们为伴侣动物提供健康和康复方面的考虑，满足它们的需求，而不仅仅是我们自己的需求时，我们

实际上也在治愈自己。事实上，我们正在治愈地球上最大弊病的主要原因之一：人类与自然的脱节。

Somewhere in the history of our species we have chosen a relationship of consumption and control rather than of

coexistence with our planet, and it seems that our goal has been to defeat or defy nature at all costs. We defy

nature’s mechanisms of resisting disease by suppressing or bypassing the immune system with corticosteroid drugs,

antibiotics, and vaccines. We ignore the natural requirements of good nutrition by supplementing an unhealthy diet

with vitamin tablets. We dam rivers and drain swamps; we even try to change the duration of daylight by resetting

the clocks for “daylight saving time.” To compound all of this heady nonsense, we have placed our own self-

imposed needs far above those of our earthly neighbors, and as a result the entire planet is suffering. For much too

long, the human condition has prohibited us from living in harmony with the natural world that surrounds us.

在我们人类历史的某个阶段，我们选择了消费和控制的关系，而不是与我们的星球共存，而且我们的目

标似乎是不惜一切代价击败或反抗自然。我们通过使用皮质类固醇药物、抗生素和疫苗来抑制或绕过免疫

系统，从而违背自然抵抗疾病的机制。我们通过用维生素片来补充不健康的饮食，从而忽视了良好营养的

自然要求。我们筑坝河流，排干沼泽；我们甚至尝试通过重置“夏令时”时钟来改变日光的持续时间。使所

Instead of studying the nature of plants from a mind-set that insists on picking their chemistries apart in an arrogant

化学成分拆开来傲慢地试图寻找可用作药物的单一化合物的心态来研究植物的本质，而是必须学会检查自

我们不能让我们的动物（我们最古老的老师）遭受难以想象的痛苦和折磨，以寻求理性的答案来满足我们

的科学需求，我们必须学会简单地接受大自然提供的自然药物。现实情况是，只有人类才需要科学验证

This is a book about a level of healing that reaches far beyond that which can be provided by science. It is about

这是一本关于远远超出科学所能提供的治疗水平的书。它是最真实意义上的整体治疗——这个过程不是

慧，我们必须重新思考我们的方式——我们必须重新学习如何奉献我们从大自然中获得的一切，我们必须

USING HERBS NATURALLY

自然使用草药

Old ways die hard—especially when we have been raised with them. In our society, mainstream approaches to

health maintenance focus on symptomatic intervention. Typically, when a person or animal gets sick, the

conventional practitioner works to identify and suppress uncomfortable or unsightly symptoms in order to achieve

immediate relief. As children, most of us are taught time and again to confront fever with pain relievers such as

aspirin, acetaminophen, or ibuprofen; dandruff with shampoos; and constipation with laxatives.

旧的生活方式很难消逝——尤其是当我们与它们一起长大时。在我们的社会中，主流的健康维护方法侧重

于对症干预。通常，当人或动物生病时，传统医生会努力识别并抑制不舒服或难看的症状，以便立即缓解

症状。作为孩子，我们大多数人都一次又一次地被教导用阿司匹林、对乙酰氨基酚或布洛芬等止痛药来应

对发烧；用洗发水去头皮屑；和泻药引起的便秘。

But what about the causes of these discomforts? Are we really taking a curative approach toward a fever if we

don’t recognize its origin and its purpose? Why do we have dandruff anyway? Why are our animals suffering with

chronic constipation? These are questions that are addressed by the holistic herbalist—one who looks at the body as

an entire, intricately balanced biocommunity of countless organs, chemicals, microorganisms, and life energies.

From a holistic perspective, the herbalist realizes that all body functions are interdependent and that physical or

emotional discomforts do not represent the totality of a health crisis but only the body’s conveyance of an

underlying imbalance or crisis—a state of “dis-ease.”

但造成这些不适的原因又是什么呢？如果我们不认识发烧的根源和目的，我们真的能对发烧采取治疗方

法吗？为什么我们会有头皮屑？为什么我们的动物患有慢性便秘？这些问题是由整体草药医生解决的，他

们将身体视为一个完整的、错综复杂的平衡生物群落，由无数器官、化学物质、微生物和生命能量组成。

从整体角度来看，中医认识到所有身体功能都是相互依存的，身体或情绪不适并不代表健康危机的全部，

而只是身体传达潜在的不平衡或危机——一种“不适”状态。

Unlike conventional Western medicine, the focus of holistic healing is not to kill or cut out disease as it occurs,

but to reestablish and maintain holistic homeostasis, the state of harmonious balance and rhythm among mind, body,

spirit, and environment. For most of us, this involves putting some old predispositions aside, revving up the

imagination, and engaging in some open-minded observation. We don’t need bioscience degrees to embrace the

principles of effective herbalism, but we are required to view health and healing from a much deeper perspective—

one that takes into account not only the discomforts of disease but also the totality of wellness. From this

perspective, for example, smoking is not a cause of lung cancer but a by-product of whatever prompts us to smoke

in the first place. Cigarettes are only a mechanism of cellular destruction, and the tumors they feed are the end

products of something insidious that lies within the psyche of the host. It is that “something” that allows us to

abandon our well-being in favor of an addictive habit we all know is bad for us, and it is from this level that the

healing process must begin.

与传统西医不同，整体治疗的重点不是在疾病发生时杀死或切除疾病，而是重建和维持整体稳态，即心

灵、身体、精神和环境之间和谐平衡和节奏的状态。对于我们大多数人来说，这需要抛开一些旧有的倾

向，激发想象力，并进行一些开放的观察。我们不需要生物科学学位来接受有效草药学的原则，但我们需

要从更深入的角度来看待健康和治疗——不仅考虑到疾病的不适，还考虑到健康的整体。例如，从这个角

度来看，吸烟并不是肺癌的原因，而是最初促使我们吸烟的事物的副产品。香烟只是细胞破坏的一种机

制，而它们所滋养的肿瘤是宿主心灵中某种阴险东西的最终产物。正是这种“东西”让我们放弃自己的幸

福，转而沉迷于我们都知道对我们有害的成瘾习惯，而治愈过程必须从这个层面开始。

Although this bit of holistic philosophy may sound simple, it is fundamentally broader than Western orthodox

medicine, which centers on intervention and subsequent suppression of disease symptoms. Western society is

spoiled by the concept of making problems go away quickly so we can get on with life. Rather than taking the

longer route toward finding a true cure, the conventional goal is to find a quick-fix solution to the inconveniences of

a crisis. Herbs are often employed in much the same capacity. The greatest healing potential of herbs, however,

emanates not from their uses as natural drug alternatives but from the holistic principles and philosophies that enable

us to use them in support of the natural healing mechanisms of the body.

尽管这种整体哲学听起来很简单，但它从根本上比西方正统医学更广泛，西方正统医学的重点是干预和

随后抑制疾病症状。西方社会被让问题迅速解决以便我们能够继续生活的观念所破坏。传统的目标不是采

取更长的路线来寻找真正的解决办法，而是找到一个快速解决危机带来的不便的解决方案。草药通常具有

大致相同的作用。然而，草药最大的治疗潜力并非源于它们作为天然药物替代品的用途，而是源于使我们

能够使用它们来支持身体自然治疗机制的整体原则和哲学。

The holistic herbalist looks beyond the symptoms of disease to identify and correct their underlying causes. An

herbalist strives to understand the harmonious checks and balances that are required among all physical and

nonphysical aspects of mind, body, spirit, and environment.

整体草药医生不仅仅关注疾病的症状，还要识别和纠正其根本原因。草药师努力理解思想、身体、精神

和环境的所有物理和非物理方面之间所需的和谐制衡。

At the core of this tightly orchestrated synergy, we find a continual need for complete nutrition because a body

must have the fuel and tools it needs to build, maintain, and repair itself. In the absence of complete nutrition,

necessary tools and building blocks are missing, and the body lacks the resources to make repairs and correct

imbalances. In addition to complete nutrition, a body sometimes requires a specialized source of stimulation or

systemic support in order to maintain a state of health and wellbeing. This is where herbs come in.

在这种紧密协调的协同作用的核心，我们发现对完整营养的持续需求，因为身体必须拥有构建、维持和

修复自身所需的燃料和工具。在缺乏完整营养的情况下，必要的工具和构建模块就会缺失，身体也缺乏修

复和纠正失衡的资源。除了完整的营养之外，身体有时还需要专门的刺激源或全身支持才能维持健康和福

祉状态。这就是草药的用武之地。

The holistic herbalist employs the chemical and energetic properties of plants to help bridge the gaps between

what a body receives from complete nutrition and what it requires from time to time in terms of supplemental

support. In this holistic context, herbs are used to stimulate, regulate, or adjust natural body functions back into

healthy harmony with the rest of the body. The therapeutic effort is directed not at treating disease but at supporting

the body in its efforts to correct the problem itself. In other words, herbs are used to assist the body naturally at what

it is designed to do: stay healthy.

整体草药师利用植物的化学和能量特性来帮助弥补身体从完整营养中获得的营养与不时需要的补充支持

之间的差距。在这种整体背景下，草药被用来刺激、调节或调整自然身体功能，使其与身体其他部位恢复

健康和谐。治疗的目的不是治疗疾病，而是支持身体努力纠正问题本身。换句话说，草药被用来帮助身体

自然地完成其设计目的：保持健康。

For many people, allowing the body to correct itself may not be easy because this requires trust in something that

still baffles our greatest scientists: the body’s remarkable, almost miraculous, ability to take care of itself. A living

body, be it animal or human, represents a system of healing and health maintenance more efficient than anything

devised by human intellect. To allow herbs to work at their optimum potential, the herb user must respect and honor

the healing powers with which we were all born.

对于许多人来说，让身体自我纠正可能并不容易，因为这需要相信仍然困扰着我们最伟大的科学家的东

西：身体非凡的、几乎是奇迹般的自我照顾能力。一个活体，无论是动物还是人类，都代表着比人类智慧

设计的任何东西都更有效的治疗和健康维护系统。为了让草药发挥最佳功效，草药使用者必须尊重和尊重

我们与生俱来的治愈能力。

THE MANY FACES OF HERBAL MEDICINE

草药的多种面貌

Many of the plants we use in Western herbalism are identical to those used in other modalities of herbal medicine.

But the philosophies of how an herb interacts with the mind, body, or spirit tend to vary greatly from culture to

culture. Here are some brief descriptions of three of the most popular forms of holistic medicine in which herbs are

commonly employed.

我们在西方草药学中使用的许多植物与其他草药疗法中使用的植物相同。但草药如何与思想、身体或精神

相互作用的哲学往往因文化而异。以下是对三种最流行的整体医学形式的简要描述，其中通常使用草药。

• Ayurvedic Medicine

• 阿育吠陀医学

In India and adjacent areas of the Middle East, ayurveda has prevailed as the primary modality of healing for

thousands of years. Ayurvedic medicine focuses on recognizing the doshas, the metabolic body type of an

individual. The first step in ayurvedic healing is to identify the specific strengths, susceptibilities, and

tendencies of the patient from a broad perspective and to take into account the entire constitution of the

individual. Once these are identified, herbs, diet, meditation, or other mechanisms are used to bring the

constitution of the individual back into harmonious balance with all elements of the mind, body, spirit, and

environment.

在印度和中东邻近地区，阿育吠陀作为主要的治疗方式已经流行了数千年。阿育吠陀医学的重点是

识别能量，即个体的代谢身体类型。阿育吠陀疗法的第一步是从广泛的角度确定患者的具体优势、

敏感性和倾向，并考虑到个人的整体体质。一旦确定了这些，就可以使用草药、饮食、冥想或其他

机制来使个体的体质恢复与思想、身体、精神和环境的所有元素的和谐平衡。

• Traditional Chinese Medicine

• 中药

Herbs have been used in traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) for at least seven thousand years. Many

principles of TCM are similar to those of ayurvedic medicine. The primary difference is in how the body is

viewed in terms of channels, rivers, winds, and energetic flows in TCM. In other words, the body is seen as a

reflection of nature, and practitioners look for energetic blockages or disruptions—dampness, dryness, hot or

cold winds, or bank breaches in the flow of qi (pronounced “chee”), the life force. The physical body is also

viewed as a set of balanced polarities: yin, which generally refers to the tissues of the body organs, and yang,

the activity of the organs. Yin and yang are opposites that cannot work independently of one another. If a yin

deficiency occurs, it is because the body does not have proper nutrients or adequate physical structure to

perform its functions. If a yang deficiency occurs, the body cannot react to metabolic stimuli. In TCM, herbs

are used to assist and maintain proper energetic flows and polarities in the body.

草药在中医 (TCM) 中的应用至少已有七千年历史。中医的许多原理与阿育吠陀医学相似。主要区别

在于中医如何看待身体的经络、河流、风和能量流。换句话说，身体被视为自然的反映，练习者寻

找能量的阻塞或破坏——潮湿、干燥、热风或冷风，或者生命力气（发音为“chee”）流动的堤坝缺

口。 。身体也被视为一组平衡的极性：阴，通常指身体器官的组织，阳，指器官的活动。阴和阳是

对立的，不能独立运作。如果出现阴虚，那是因为身体没有适当的营养或足够的身体结构来发挥其

功能。如果出现阳虚，身体就无法对代谢刺激做出反应。在中医中，草药用于协助和维持体内适当

的能量流动和极性。

=== PAGE 24 ===
Traditional herbal cabinet at a Chinese pharmacy

中药房的传统草药柜

• Western Herbalism

• 西方草药学

In contrast, Western herbalism seems almost superficial in nature. Western herbalism originates from ancient

uses of medicinal plants in Europe. Many of the principles, philosophies, and certainly our validations of

how herbs are used to effect healing are constantly evolving in this form of herbalism. For instance, the

spirituality of the healer, the patient, and even the herb itself was once the primary focus of herbal medicine

in ancient Europe. But today, Western herbalists incorporate many philosophies, including scientific

validation of photochemical compounds, plant energetics, folkloric accounts and belief systems, and several

other points of opinion.

相比之下，西方草药学本质上似乎几乎是肤浅的。西方草药学起源于欧洲古代对药用植物的使用。

许多原则、哲学，当然还有我们对如何使用草药来实现治疗效果的验证，都在这种形式的草药学中

不断发展。例如，治疗者、病人、甚至草药本身的灵性曾经是古代欧洲草药的主要关注点。但今

天，西方草药学家融合了许多哲学，包括光化学化合物的科学验证、植物能量学、民间传说和信仰

体系，以及其他一些观点。

As Western herbalists, we base our use of herbs on a balance of all philosophies. We respect and admire

recent scientific validations of medicinal plant chemistries, but we also strongly believe that plants contain

synergistic balances of chemical, energetic, and perhaps spiritual elements that make them unique and

unexplainable. We see a great deal of value in much of the anecdotal evidence that has been handed down

regarding the traditional uses of herbs over the past few millennia. Although scientific studies have failed to

validate many of the claims that have been passed down through the ages, the fact that many of these

customs have worked safely and effectively for thousands of people throughout several centuries is certainly

convincing to us. But despite differences in opinion, most Western herbalists share a similar, holistic

perspective when it comes to doing the actual work of healing.

作为西方草药师，我们将草药的使用建立在所有哲学的平衡之上。我们尊重并钦佩最近对药用植

物化学的科学验证，但我们也坚信植物含有化学、能量、或许还有精神元素的协同平衡，这使得它

们独特且无法解释。我们在过去几千年流传下来的有关草药传统用途的许多轶事证据中看到了很大

的价值。尽管科学研究未能证实许多流传已久的说法，但其中许多习俗在几个世纪以来对成千上万

的人安全有效地发挥作用这一事实无疑让我们信服。尽管观点存在差异，但大多数西方草药医生在

进行实际治疗工作时都持有相似的整体观点。

The body is viewed from a biological perspective but with a focus that takes into account the totality of the

individual. While mainstream modalities of Western medicine focus primarily on the treatment of disease

=== PAGE 25 ===
and suppression of symptoms with little regard to cause, the herbalist works from the opposite direction.

While working to promote health by addressing the underlying causes and providing aid to the body’s

efforts, the Western herbalist views the body as a tightly knit biosystem of organs, cooperative cells,

microbes, enzymes, nutrients, and synergistic energies that must be maintained in a state of cooperative

balance. During a disease crisis, herbs are utilized to strengthen or stimulate the body’s natural functions at

chemical and energetic levels so that a state of health can be reestablished quickly and efficiently. After the

crisis is over, herbal tonics may then be used to strengthen body functions that are chronically deficient to

avoid reoccurrence.

从生物学角度看待身体，但重点考虑到个体的整体性。西医的主流治疗方法主要侧重于治疗疾病

和抑制症状，很少考虑病因，而草药师则从相反的方向进行治疗。在通过解决根本原因和为身体提

供帮助来促进健康的同时，西方草药师将身体视为一个由器官、合作细胞、微生物、酶、营养物质

和协同能量组成的紧密结合的生物系统，必须在合作平衡状态。在疾病危机期间，草药被用来在化

学和能量水平上增强或刺激身体的自然功能，以便快速有效地恢复健康状态。危机结束后，可以使

用草药补品来增强长期缺乏的身体功能，以避免再次发生。

While the philosophies that lead people to the use of herbal medicines are variable worldwide, all

modalities of herbal healing share two fundamental similarities. One is that the therapeutic focus is holistic,

taking into account the totality of the individual instead of the symptoms of disease only. The other is that all

good herbalists know that herbs work best in a proactive capacity when employed from a perspective that

recognizes health maintenance as the paramount cure for disease.

虽然世界各地引导人们使用草药的理念各不相同，但所有草药治疗方式都有两个基本相似之处。

一是治疗重点是整体的，考虑个体的整体，而不仅仅是疾病的症状。另一个是，所有优秀的草药医

生都知道，当从认识到维持健康是治疗疾病的首要方法的角度出发时，草药以积极主动的方式发挥

最佳作用。

HERBS AS ALTERNATIVES TO CONVENTIONAL MEDICINES

草药作为传统药物的替代品

Many of us are introduced to the realm of herbal medicine by using herbs as direct replacements for over-the-

counter or prescription drugs. Like drugs, herbs can be used to treat the symptoms of disease effectively. Unlike

many drugs, herbs are relatively safe and gentle medicines—they are very forgiving, offering a much greater margin

of error and fewer adverse side effects.

我们中的许多人通过使用草药作为非处方药或处方药的直接替代品而进入草药领域。像药物一样，草药可

以用来有效治疗疾病的症状。与许多药物不同，草药是相对安全且温和的药物——它们非常宽容，提供更

大的误差范围和更少的不良副作用。

Most drugs are composed of specific chemical compounds that have been isolated from their source and

concentrated to maximum potency. A medicinal plant, however, consists of dozens, sometimes thousands, of

interactive or inert chemical components. Many skeptics argue that herbal medicines are less effective and unsafe

because the concentrations of active constituents are too low and are variable from plant to plant.

大多数药物由特定的化合物组成，这些化合物已从其来源中分离出来并浓缩至最大效力。然而，药用植

物由数十种，有时甚至数千种相互作用或惰性化学成分组成。许多怀疑论者认为，草药的功效较差且不安

全，因为活性成分的浓度太低，并且植物与植物之间的浓度存在差异。

To the herbalist, the presence of scientifically proven compounds is only part of what makes a plant useful.

Instead of focusing on isolated chemical components, the herbalist accepts the inexplicable synergy that exists

among all components of a plant’s chemistry and all components of the physical and nonphysical recipient. In the

mind of the herbalist, this is what makes herbal medicine safe, effective, and unique. The whole plant is always

greater, and usually safer, than the sum of its parts.

对于草药师来说，经科学证明的化合物的存在只是植物有用的一部分。草药师不关注孤立的化学成分，

而是接受植物化学的所有成分以及物理和非物理接受者的所有成分之间存在的难以解释的协同作用。在草

药医生看来，这就是草药安全、有效和独特的原因。整个工厂总是比其各个部分的总和更大，而且通常更

安全。

For those who are trying to break away from conventional ways of thinking, this concept of holistic synergy can

be difficult to grasp. Having been raised and trained in a science-based culture, accepting something that cannot be

fully rationalized can be difficult. But to put things into a scientific perspective, let’s look at thymol, the primary

active constituent of thyme (Thymus spp.).

对于那些试图摆脱传统思维方式的人来说，整体协同的概念可能很难理解。在以科学为基础的文化中长

大和接受训练的人，接受一些不能完全合理化的事情可能会很困难。但为了从科学的角度来看，我们来看

看百里香酚，它是百里香（百里香属）的主要活性成分。

Thymol is potentially toxic when isolated from the rest of the thyme plant. But when employed as part of the

whole plant in a tincture or tea, thymol serves as an active part of a safe and effective antimicrobial, dewormer, and

cough suppressant medicine.

当从百里香植物的其余部分中分离出百里香酚时，它具有潜在的毒性。但当百里香酚作为整个植物的一

部分用于酊剂或茶中时，它就成为安全有效的抗菌、驱虫和止咳药物的活性部分。

Anybody from any discipline of science can pick up a simple herbal remedy and use it for the purpose of treating

illness. It’s really very easy to substitute many of the favored conventional medicines with herbal remedies. But here

are a few important things to remember.

任何科学学科的任何人都可以选择一种简单的草药并用它来治疗疾病。用草药替代许多受欢迎的传统药

物确实非常容易。但这里有一些需要记住的重要事项。

• Keep in mind that herbs are slower acting than most drugs. Expectation of rapid results is perhaps the greatest

cause of frustration and failure among would-be herbalists. The difference between a successful herbal

therapy and resorting to a shot of, say, prednisolone often amounts to a day or two of patient waiting.

• 请记住，草药的作用比大多数药物要慢。对快速结果的期望可能是潜在的草药师沮丧和失败的最大原

=== PAGE 28 ===
因。成功的草药疗法和注射泼尼松龙之类的药物之间的区别通常相当于患者等待一两天。

• When using herbs as direct replacements for allopathic medicines, don’t expect results beyond those you

would expect from the drugs you are replacing. The only difference in therapy when using herbs as drug

substitutes is the medicinal device; the curative depth of the therapy remains the same.

• 当使用草药作为对抗疗法药物的直接替代品时，不要期望超出您所替代药物的预期结果。使用草药作

为药物替代品时，治疗的唯一区别在于医疗器械；治疗的治疗深度保持不变。

• If you opt to use herbs symptomatically, it is important to remember that you will likely end up discouraged if

you expect to find a cure. For example, when treating conjunctivitis that is secondary to bacterial infection, a

combination eyewash of Oregon grape (Mahonia aquifolium ), raspberry leaf (Rubus idaeus), and sterile

saline will effectively replace most conventional ophthalmic preparations—but just like a conventional

preparation, the herbs won’t address the underlying causes of a chronic problem.

• 如果您选择对症使用草药，请务必记住，如果您希望找到治疗方法，您可能最终会灰心丧气。例如，

在治疗继发于细菌感染的结膜炎时，俄勒冈葡萄（Mahonia aquifolium）、覆盆子叶（Rubus idaeus）

和无菌盐水的组合洗眼液将有效取代大多数传统的眼科制剂，但就像传统制剂一样，草药不能解决

慢性问题的根本原因。

=== PAGE 29 ===
HERB ACTIONS AND SPECIAL AFFINITIES

草药的作用和特殊的亲和力

It is unrealistic to think a full conveyance of effective herbal wisdom can be contained in this book, but a large

measure of awareness can be perpetuated by embracing a basic understanding of how each of these plants works

within the body. In Western herbalism, the effects that plant materials have in or on the body are called “medicinal

actions” or “active properties.” By becoming familiar with the medicinal actions of the herbs to which you have

access, you will have a good idea where to look for an appropriate course of therapy when a need for one arises. In

addition to knowing the manner by which herbs work in the body, it is also important to begin learning each herb’s

specialty, or systemic affinity—its special kinship with certain portions of the anatomy. For instance, we may know

that slippery elm has a general astringent action (meaning that it shrinks tissues), but its effective usefulness can be

really pronounced when we know that it has a special affinity to the digestive tract, where its astringent actions are

particularly well suited to shrinking the inner wall of the small intestine to relieve diarrhea and other discomforts.

认为本书能够全面传达有效的草药智慧是不现实的，但通过对每种植物如何在体内发挥作用的基本了解，

可以在很大程度上保持这种意识。在西方草药学中，植物材料对身体的作用被称为“药用作用”或“活性特

性”。通过熟悉您可以获得的草药的药用作用，您将清楚地知道在需要时到哪里寻找合适的治疗方案。除了

了解草药在体内的作用方式之外，开始了解每种草药的特殊性或系统亲和力（其与解剖学某些部分的特殊

亲缘关系）也很重要。例如，我们可能知道滑榆具有一般的收敛作用（意味着它会收缩组织），但当我们

知道它对消化道有特殊的亲和力时，它的有效用处才真正明显，而在消化道中，它的收敛作用尤其明显。

非常适合收缩小肠内壁以缓解腹泻和其他不适。

DOSAGE AND DURATION OF THERAPY

剂量和治疗持续时间

The dosage suggestions provided in this book represent what we feel are safe and conservative starting points for

use in most animals. The exact dosage and duration of an herb therapy that your companion may need depends on

the animal’s specific needs, tolerances, and metabolism. In other words, the answers to how much and for how long

may vary from animal to animal.

本书中提供的剂量建议代表了我们认为对大多数动物使用安全且保守的起点。您的同伴可能需要的草药疗

法的确切剂量和持续时间取决于动物的具体需求、耐受性和新陈代谢。换句话说，关于多少和持续多久的

答案可能因动物而异。

Some animals respond favorably to very small doses—perhaps just a drop or two of tincture. Others require larger

doses or may not respond to certain herbs at all (as you know, such is the case with drugs too). Therefore, a

conservative starting point for administration of herb extracts, infusions, or dried herbs in dogs, cats, and herbivores

is to use only one or two herbs at a time and to proportion the dosage based on the animal’s body weight compared

to the recommended human dosage. For example, a 30-pound dog would receive one-fifth of that which is

recommended for a 150-pound human. Also to be considered is your veterinarian’s opinion, a reputable reference

book, or the product manufacturer’s recommendations.

有些动物对非常小的剂量（也许只是一两滴酊剂）有良好的反应。其他人则需要更大的剂量，或者可能

对某些草药根本没有反应（如您所知，药物也是如此）。因此，对狗、猫和食草动物施用草药提取物、输

液或干草药的保守起点是一次仅使用一种或两种草药，并根据动物体重与推荐剂量相比来调整剂量。人体

剂量。例如，一只 30 磅重的狗所接受的剂量仅为 150 磅重人类建议剂量的五分之一。还需要考虑的是兽医

的意见、信誉良好的参考书或产品制造商的建议。

Remember, this is just a starting point. Dogs, cats, and other carnivores have much faster metabolic rates than we

do; therefore, initial dosages might have to be increased later to achieve the results you are looking for. The biggest

mistake is to think of dosing in terms of absolutes. Instead, watch the animal you are treating; read up on the side

effects, contraindications, and active nature of the herbs you are using; and don’t hesitate to change dosages. If you

need to increase a dosage, do so in 10 percent increments to a maximum of 50 percent above the starting dose. In

other words, if you have determined that the starting dose for “Max” is 20 drops of burdock, twice daily, then you

can increase the dose 2 drops at a time until you reach 30 drops, if necessary. If a dosage needs to be decreased (if,

for example, valerian causes acute vomiting in your cat), cut the dose in half. If you feel it’s necessary, stop the

therapy altogether for a day or two, and let the animal’s body readjust before proceeding with the reduced dosage.

Most animals require a dose two to three times daily.

请记住，这只是一个起点。狗、猫和其他食肉动物的新陈代谢率比我们快得多；因此，以后可能需要增

加初始剂量才能达到您想要的结果。最大的错误是从绝对角度考虑剂量。相反，要注意你正在治疗的动

物；了解您正在使用的草药的副作用、禁忌症和活性性质；并且不要犹豫改变剂量。如果您需要增加剂

=== PAGE 38 ===
量，请以 10% 的增量进行，最多比起始剂量高 50%。换句话说，如果您确定“Max”的起始剂量是 20 滴牛

蒡，每天两次，那么您可以每次增加 2 滴剂量，直到达到 30 滴（如有必要）。如果需要减少剂量（例如，

缬草导致猫急性呕吐），请将剂量减半。如果您觉得有必要，请完全停止治疗一两天，让动物的身体重新

调整，然后再继续减少剂量。大多数动物每天需要服用两到三次。

The duration of an herbal therapy also depends on the specific animal and varies according to the disease you are

confronting. Generally, it is best to take at least a two-day break from herbal therapies each week (five days on, two

days off). This allows you to monitor the animal’s responses to the herbs and to alleviate any tolerance or toxicity

problems she may otherwise develop as a result of long-term use. The duration required to see results varies greatly

and is dependent on the nature of the herb, the animal, and the severity of the imbalance you are confronting. If

results don’t begin to materialize after you have maintained a maximum dosage schedule for more than seven days,

it may be time to try another herb or to consult your holistic veterinarian. In any case, keep detailed records of your

successes, failures, and observations. Exactly how long to maintain an herbal therapy can be determined only

through experience and familiarity with your animal, and good record keeping is instrumental to becoming an

effective herbalist.

草药治疗的持续时间还取决于具体的动物，并根据您所面临的疾病而有所不同。一般来说，最好每周停

止草药治疗至少休息两天（连续五天，休息两天）。这使您可以监测动物对草药的反应，并减轻她因长期

使用而可能出现的任何耐受性或毒性问题。看到结果所需的时间差异很大，具体取决于草药、动物的性质

以及您所面临的不平衡的严重程度。如果在您维持最大剂量计划超过 7 天后仍未开始显现结果，则可能是

时候尝试另一种草药或咨询您的整体兽医了。无论如何，详细记录你的成功、失败和观察结果。草药治疗

的确切维持时间只能通过经验和对动物的熟悉程度来确定，而良好的记录保存有助于成为一名有效的草药

师。

=== PAGE 39 ===
A FEW WORDS ABOUT TOXICITY

关于毒性的几句话

Serious adverse reactions are rare, but when used outside the parameters of common sense and moderation, any

plant can be toxic.

严重的不良反应很少见，但如果超出常识和适度的范围使用，任何植物都可能有毒。

Toxicity is dose dependent, relative to the rate of absorption and the individual’s ability to assimilate or eliminate

an excess. If a body receives a substance in quantities or concentrations that cannot be effectively dealt with by its

natural functions, the excess must be dealt with by emergency means. Vomiting, diarrhea, and other purgative

functions are then triggered to eliminate the invasive substance(s). If this fails, systemic shutdown or damage may

occur.

毒性是剂量依赖性的，与吸收率和个体吸收或消除过量的能力有关。如果身体接收到的物质的数量或浓

度无法通过其自然功能有效处理，则必须通过紧急手段处理过量的物质。然后触发呕吐、腹泻和其他泻下

功能以消除侵入性物质。如果失败，可能会发生系统关闭或损坏。

Most herbs that are commonly used in veterinary medicine are safe and forgiving—in most cases in which an

animal is hypersensitive to an herb or has received too much, she will vomit shortly after administration. Other

common indicators of toxicity include itching, photosensitivity, and diarrhea.

大多数兽医常用的草药都是安全且宽容的——在大多数情况下，动物对草药过敏或服用过多草药，在给

药后不久就会呕吐。其他常见的毒性指标包括瘙痒、光敏性和腹泻。

The key word in the avoidance of toxic reactions is moderation. Although herbs are generally weaker and gentler

medicines than most drugs, they still demand respect. “More” is not necessarily “better,” even in the employment of

nutritive “food-medicine” herbs such as nettle (Urtica spp.), alfalfa (Medicago sativa), or flaxseed (Linum spp.). All

of these herbs may cause digestive upset and dermatological reactions if fed to the animal in large quantities.

避免毒性反应的关键词是适度。尽管草药通常是比大多数药物更弱、更温和的药物，但它们仍然需要尊

重。 “更多”不一定是“更好”，即使是在使用营养性“食药”草药时，如荨麻 (Urtica spp.)、苜蓿 (Medicago

sativa) 或亚麻籽 (Linum spp.)。如果大量喂给动物，所有这些草药都可能导致消化不良和皮肤反应。

Aside from the issues of overdose and prolonged use, it is important to remember that some animals may have

allergies to certain herbs; a few are especially sensitive to certain plant substances; and some have preexisting

conditions. Therefore, to be safe, it’s always a good idea to proceed with caution. Start with a small dose, and watch

the animal for any signs of adverse reaction.

除了过量和长期使用的问题外，重要的是要记住，一些动物可能对某些草药过敏；少数对某些植物物质

特别敏感；有些人有既往病史。因此，为了安全起见，谨慎行事总是一个好主意。从小剂量开始，观察动

物是否有任何不良反应迹象。

=== PAGE 40 ===
WHEN TO TAKE YOUR PET TO THE VET

何时带您的宠物去看兽医

This book is aimed at enabling you to be somewhat self-sufficient in ensuring the health and welfare of your

companion animals. However, there are some problems that caregivers should not attempt to treat on their own at

home. Some of these include life-threatening situations such as poisonings; major traumas such as those caused by

being hit by a car; bleeding; broken bones; instances when the condition you’re treating at home doesn’t get better in

a few days; and cases in which there are questions or other avenues of treatment to be taken.

本书的目的是使您能够在一定程度上自给自足，确保您的伴侣动物的健康和福利。然而，有一些问题护理

人员不应尝试在家中自行处理。其中一些包括危及生命的情况，例如中毒；重大创伤，例如被车撞造成的

创伤；流血的;骨折；您在家治疗的病情几天内没有好转的情况；以及存在疑问或需要采取其他治疗途径的

情况。

Most of us believe that our animals must be seen by a vet in order to get treatment. In many cases this is true. But

holistic vets can’t be found in all areas of the U.S., so it becomes necessary for some of us to consult with a vet over

the telephone. Some holistic veterinarians do provide telephone consultations, but many don’t. No matter, it’s wise

to have a local vet to whom you can take your animals in case of a major trauma or if surgery is needed.

我们大多数人都认为，我们的动物必须去看兽医才能得到治疗。在许多情况下这是事实。但并非在美国

所有地区都能找到全面的兽医，因此我们中的一些人有必要通过电话咨询兽医。一些整体兽医确实提供电

话咨询，但很多不提供。无论如何，明智的做法是聘请当地的兽医，您可以在动物遭受重大创伤或需要手

术时将其带到他那里。

=== PAGE 41 ===
CAUTIONS, CONTRAINDICATIONS, AND POTENTIAL SIDE

EFFECTS

注意事项、禁忌症和潜在副作用

The following chart lists a few of the most common types of problematic plant compounds to be aware of in

the natural care of animals. This list is intended for the purpose of cautious awareness. It is by no means

complete, and the presence of one or more of these compounds in a specific herb does not necessarily

exclude that herb from safe use.

下表列出了在动物自然护理中需要注意的一些最常见的有问题的植物化合物类型。此列表旨在供谨

慎认识之用。它绝不是完整的，并且特定草药中存在一种或多种这些化合物并不一定排除该草药的

安全使用。

Anthraquinones

蒽醌类

Anthraquinones, including dianthrone glycosides, sennosides, aloe-emoden, chysophanol, among others, are

the active laxative constituents that are present in aloe (certain preparations), senna (Cassia senna), cascara

sagrada, and turkey rhubarb (Rheum palmatum). Anthraquinones act as laxatives by stimulating intestinal

peristalsis and may cause cramping and severe diarrhea if misused. These compounds are hard on the liver

and kidneys, and extended use of anthraquinone-bearing herbs may lead to dependency.

蒽醌，包括二蒽酮糖苷、番泻苷、芦荟大黄素、糜酚等，是芦荟（某些制剂）、番泻叶（决明）、

鼠李皮和火鸡大黄（大黄）中存在的活性泻药成分。蒽醌通过刺激肠道蠕动起到泻药的作用，如果

使用不当可能会导致痉挛和严重腹泻。这些化合物对肝脏和肾脏不利，长期使用含蒽醌的草药可能

会导致依赖性。

Coumarins

香豆素类

Coumarins include coumarin, medicagol, furanocoumarins, among others. Most coumarin-bearing plants do

not contain enough coumarins to represent a risk in normal therapeutic doses. Large doses of coumarins,

however, can cause photosensitivity. Coumarins are known to thin the blood and may potentiate the effects

of anticoagulant drugs. Coumarin-rich herbs such as red clover (Trifolium pratense) and alfalfa (Medicago

sativa) should not be given to animals with clotting disorders.

香豆素类包括香豆素、medicagol、呋喃香豆素等。大多数含香豆素的植物不含足够的香豆素，不足

以代表正常治疗剂量的风险。然而，大剂量的香豆素会引起光敏性。众所周知，香豆素可以稀释血

液，并可能增强抗凝药物的作用。富含香豆素的草药，如红三叶草（Trifolium pratense）和苜蓿

（Medicago sativa）不应给患有凝血障碍的动物服用。

Oxalic Acid and Oxalates

草酸和草酸盐

Oxalic acid and oxalates are present in many plants (a small amount is even present in fresh spinach), but can

be found especially in members of the Polygonaceae and Cruciferae families. Oxalic acid is characterized by

a tart, lemony flavor and is especially evident in the leaves of sheep sorrel (Rumex acetosella) and French

sorrel (Rumex scutatus ). Oxalic acid can cause urinary tract irritation, can deplete the body of vitamin B1,

and is known to bind with calcium in the urine—thus potentially causing stones. Although the oxalic acid

content of most herbs, such as yellow dock root (Rumex crispus ), is generally small and usually will not

cause a problem with moderately dosed, short-term use (up to fourteen days), it is best to avoid such herbs in

cases of preexisting kidney or urinary disease.

草酸和草酸盐存在于许多植物中（少量甚至存在于新鲜菠菜中），但尤其存在于蓼科和十字花科的

成员中。草酸的特点是酸、柠檬味，在羊酢浆草 (Rumex acetosella) 和法国酢浆草 (Rumex scutatus) 的

=== PAGE 42 ===
叶子中尤其明显。草酸会引起尿路刺激，会消耗体内的维生素 B1，并且会与尿液中的钙结合，从而

可能导致结石。虽然大多数草药（如黄酸模）的草酸含量一般很少，并且中等剂量、短期使用（最

多十四天）通常不会造成问题，但最好避免使用这种草酸。用于治疗已有肾脏或泌尿系统疾病的草

药。

Pyrrolizidine Alkaloids

吡咯里西啶生物碱

Pyrrolizidine alkaloids are present in many plants but most notably in comfrey (Symphytum officinale). Most

PA-bearing plants have received an undeserved bad name; it takes doses that are dozens of times in excess of

a therapeutic quantity to cause hepatotoxic effects—especially in a healthy liver. Nonetheless, there are

documented cases of liver damage (in both human and animal modalities) as a result of comfrey overuse.

吡咯里西啶生物碱存在于许多植物中，但最著名的是紫草（Symphytum officinale）。大多数含有 PA

的植物都受到了不应有的坏名声。需要超出治疗量数十倍的剂量才会引起肝毒性作用，尤其是在健

康的肝脏中。尽管如此，有记录表明过度使用紫草会导致肝损伤（人类和动物）。

There are hundreds of different alkaloid compounds present in thousands of medicinal plant species—many

are generally safe; some present a risk of toxicity. Many present themselves as the primary active constituent

of a plant. Perhaps the most frequently employed alkaloid in Western herbal medicine is berberine, the bitter

yellow substance that is found in Oregon grape (Mahonia spp.), goldenseal (Hydrastis canadensis), and a

few other plants. Berberine is generally safe, but overuse of berberine-rich plants may overstimulate bile

production (especially in cats), resulting in vomiting. Berberine is contraindicated in pregnant or lactating

animals.

数千种药用植物中存在数百种不同的生物碱化合物，其中许多通常是安全的；有些存在中毒风险。

许多本身就是植物的主要活性成分。也许西方草药中最常用的生物碱是小檗碱，这是一种苦黄色物

质，存在于俄勒冈葡萄（Mahonia spp.）、白毛茛（Hydrastis canadensis）和其他一些植物中。小檗

碱通常是安全的，但过度使用富含小檗碱的植物可能会过度刺激胆汁产生（尤其是猫），导致呕

吐。小檗碱禁用于怀孕或哺乳期动物。

Salicylates

水杨酸盐

Salicylates, including salicylaldehyde, salicin, methyl salicylate, salicylic acid, among others, are the

precursors to acetylsalicylate (aspirin). This means that herbs such as willow bark (Salix spp.), meadowsweet

(Filipendula ulmaria), poplar (Populus spp.), and others must be used with extreme caution in felines or

other animals who are sensitive to aspirin.

水杨酸盐，包括水杨醛、水杨苷、水杨酸甲酯、水杨酸等，是乙酰水杨酸盐（阿司匹林）的前体。

这意味着，对于猫科动物或其他对阿司匹林敏感的动物，必须极其谨慎地使用柳树皮（Salix

spp.）、绣线菊（Filipendula ulmaria）、杨树（Populus spp.）等草药。

Saponins

皂甙

There are hundreds of different saponin (soaplike) constituents in various plants. Most notably, saponins are

among the primary active constituents in valerian (Valeriana officinalis ), licorice (Glycyrrhiza spp.),

sarsaparilla (Smilax spp.), and yucca root (Yucca spp.). Saponins are characterized by their foaming, soapy

nature. Although they seldom present any problems, excessive or extended use of saponin-rich herbs can

produce GI irritation and vomiting, and some may eventually interfere with the absorption of fat-soluble

vitamins.

各种植物中有数百种不同的皂苷（肥皂样）成分。最值得注意的是，皂苷是缬草 (Valeriana

officinalis)、甘草 (Glycyrrhiza spp.)、菝葜 (Smilax spp.) 和丝兰根 (Yucca spp.) 的主要活性成分之一。

皂苷的特点是具有泡沫、肥皂性质。虽然它们很少出现任何问题，但过量或长期使用富含皂苷的草

药会导致胃肠道刺激和呕吐，有些可能最终会干扰脂溶性维生素的吸收。

=== PAGE 43 ===
Sterols

甾醇

Sterols include ß-sitosterol, stigmasterol, ampesterol, among others. Some plants, such as licorice, that

contain large concentrations of phytosterols or steroidal saponins can cause problems, such as water retention

and hypertension, similar to those presented by steroidal drugs but only if used excessively or over an

extended period. The side effects of phytosterols are much harder to procure, and can be largely avoided by

occasional breaks in the therapy (for example, five days on, two off) and with concurrent use of diuretic

herbs such as dandelion leaf and alterative herbs such as dandelion root and burdock.

甾醇包括β-谷甾醇、豆甾醇、ampesterol等。一些植物，如甘草，含有高浓度的植物甾醇或甾体皂

苷，可能会引起问题，如水潴留和高血压，类似于甾体药物所带来的问题，但只有在过量或长时间

使用的情况下才会出现。植物甾醇的副作用更难获得，并且可以通过偶尔中断治疗（例如，使用五

天，休息两天）并同时使用利尿草药（例如蒲公英叶）和替代草药（例如蒲公英）来很大程度上避

免根和牛蒡。

Tannins

单宁

Tannins such as corilagin pyranoside, ellagic acid, and gallic acid are found in the bark and leaves of many

herbs and are the most frequently employed astringents of the plant world. Herbs that are especially tannin

rich include uva ursi (Arctostaph los uva-ursi ), any part of the juniper (Juniperis spp.) plant, black walnut

hulls (Juglans nigra), and white oak bark (Quercus sp.). Tannins are typically used to reduce inflammations

of mucous membranes in the digestive and urinary tracts, but if used excessively they can have a reverse

effect, causing mucosal irritation. Herbs that contain tannins should not be used in animals with

inflammatory kidney disease. Some tannins are labor inducing (oxytocic) and may cause abortion in

pregnant animals.

单宁如吡喃柯里拉苷、鞣花酸和没食子酸存在于许多草药的树皮和叶子中，是植物界最常用的收敛

剂。单宁含量特别丰富的草本植物包括熊果 (Arctostaph los uva-ursi)、杜松 (Juniperis spp.) 植物的任

何部分、黑胡桃壳 (Juglans nigra) 和白橡树皮 (Quercus sp.)。单宁通常用于减少消化道和泌尿道粘膜

的炎症，但如果使用过量，可能会产生相反的效果，导致粘膜刺激。含有单宁的草药不应用于患有

炎症性肾病的动物。有些单宁具有引产作用（催产作用），可能会导致怀孕动物流产。

Volatile Oils

挥发油

Volatile oils include myristicin, apiole, terpineol, sesquiterpenes, menthone, pulegone, piperidinone, thujone,

jugulone, 3-octanol, among others. There are hundreds of volatile oil compounds, many of which make up

the aromatic principles of a plant, present in thousands of plant species. Menthol, for example, is a volatile

oil found in members of the mint family. The medicinal activities and toxicology of volatile oils are widely

variable, but most have an effect on the genitourinary and digestive tracts, causing irritation to the kidneys

and urinary passages when used in large quantities. Others, such as the pulegone found in pennyroyal

(Mentha pulegium) or the myristicin and apiole found in parsley seed (Petroselinum crispum) and nutmeg

seed (Myristica fragrans), are potentially hepatotoxic and nephrotoxic if used in overabundance. Volatile oils

have been shown to cross the placenta barrier to adversely affect the fetus of pregnant animals.

挥发油包括肉豆蔻苷、芹菜酮、萜品醇、倍半萜烯、薄荷酮、胡薄荷酮、哌啶酮、侧柏酮、胡古

酮、3-辛醇等。有数百种挥发油化合物，其中许多构成植物的芳香成分，存在于数千种植物中。例

如，薄荷醇是在薄荷家族成员中发现的一种挥发油。挥发油的药用活性和毒理学差异很大，但大多

数对泌尿生殖道和消化道有影响，大量使用时会刺激肾脏和尿道。其他物质，例如薄荷醇（Mentha

pulegium）中发现的胡薄荷酮或欧芹种子（Petroselinum Criscum）和肉豆蔻种子（Myristica

fragrans）中发现的肉豆蔻苷和芹菜籽，如果过量使用，则可能具有肝毒性和肾毒性。挥发油已被证

明可以穿过胎盘屏障，对怀孕动物的胎儿产生不利影响。

The s-methyl cysteine sulfoxide and n-propyl disuldhide contained in garlic has been shown to produce

=== PAGE 44 ===
Heinz-body anemia, a serious blood disorder, if the cloves are consumed in excess of 0.5 percent of the

subject animal’s body weight. This means that a healthy 60-pound dog would have to eat several cloves of

garlic just to start the Heinz-body process. The problem is dose dependent, meaning that blood structure

quickly normalizes when garlic use is reduced or discontinued.

大蒜中含有的 s-甲基半胱氨酸亚砜和正丙基二硫醚已被证明，如果大蒜的食用量超过对象动物体

重的 0.5%，就会导致亨氏体贫血，这是一种严重的血液疾病。这意味着一只 60 磅重的健康狗必须

吃几瓣大蒜才能开始亨氏体过程。这个问题与剂量有关，这意味着当减少或停止使用大蒜时，血液

结构会迅速恢复正常。

=== PAGE 45 ===
BASICS OF HERBAL PREPARATIONS

草药制剂的基础知识

The manner in which an herb is used is determined by a holistic assessment of the particular circumstances at hand

and the overall nature of the animal. Once you have investigated the origins of the symptoms that have caught your

attention, you can select the medicinal actions you need to confront the problem. This leads you to one or more

herbs that have a specific affinity to the body systems that are involved.

草药的使用方式取决于对当前特定情况和动物整体性质的整体评估。一旦您调查了引起您注意的症状的根

源，您就可以选择解决问题所需的药物措施。这会让您找到一种或多种对所涉及的身体系统具有特定亲和

力的草药。

Choosing the correct herb to fit therapeutic circumstances is critical not only to the effective treatment of disease

but also to the conservation of botanical resources. Many plant species are currently at risk of extinction because

they have been touted as “curative silver bullets.” But in reality, there are no cure-all herbs. In fact, no single herb

serves as a definitive cure for anything. For an herb to be used effectively and responsibly, it should be used only

within the true confines of its therapeutic capacity. It also must be used in a form or preparation that is

complementary to its medicinal attributes and the task at hand.

选择适合治疗环境的正确草药不仅对于有效治疗疾病而且对于保护植物资源也至关重要。许多植物物种

目前面临灭绝的危险，因为它们被吹捧为“治疗灵丹妙药”。但实际上，没有包治百病的草药。事实上，没

有任何一种草药可以包治百病。为了有效和负责任地使用草药，它应该只在其治疗能力的真正范围内使

用。它还必须以与其药用属性和当前任务相补充的形式或制剂使用。

Each herb’s physical and chemical structures determine how the herb should be prepared and subsequently

administered. For instance, many herbs are very water soluble, which means that if you pour hot water over them,

their medicinal constituents quickly and completely infuse into the water, making their desired chemical attributes

freely available for the body to absorb and use. Many other herbs, however, are poorly water soluble, which means

that if you pour hot water over them to make an infusion, little or nothing of medicinal value is drawn from the

plant’s tissues.

每种草药的物理和化学结构决定了如何制备和随后服用。例如，许多草药都是非常水溶性的，这意味着

如果你将热水倒在它们上面，它们的药用成分会迅速而完全地注入水中，使其所需的化学属性可以自由地

供人体吸收和使用。然而，许多其他草药的水溶性较差，这意味着如果将热水倒在它们上进行输液，从植

物组织中提取的药用价值很少或根本没有。

Following is an introduction to the basic how-tos of making herbal preparations. Those of you who collect books

will find that compared to other books on herbal medicines, the guidelines we offer here are loose. We have done

this for the sake of practicality and simplicity. While exact measurements and strict procedures are necessary

measures of quality control in the commercial production of herbal products, the self-reliant herbalist really doesn’t

have to worry so much about precision. As long as there’s enough herb, a strong-enough solvent, and the correct

type of preparation, you will be rewarded with a good, strong herbal medicine.

以下是制作草药制剂的基本方法的介绍。收藏书籍的人会发现，与其他草药书籍相比，我们这里提供的

指导方针比较宽松。我们这样做是为了实用性和简单性。虽然精确的测量和严格的程序是草药产品商业生

产中质量控制的必要措施，但自力更生的草药师实际上不必太担心精度。只要有足够的草药、足够强的溶

剂和正确的制剂类型，你就会得到一种好的、强效的草药。

=== PAGE 46 ===
DRIED BULK HERB MATERIAL

干散装药草材料

Dried bulk herbs are handy to have around because they allow for a great deal of diversity in how they can be

prepared and applied. In addition to being used in various herb preparations, some dried herbs can be sprinkled

directly onto an animal’s food. As a general rule, roots keep two to three times longer than dried leaf material. But

don’t stock up on more than you can use within one year, and be sure to store your herbs in airtight containers that

are kept away from sunlight. Regardless of proper storage methods, dried herbs eventually oxidize and lose their

potency. A few herbs lose much of their medicinal and nutritive value within days of drying. Buy herbs from an

honest, knowledgeable herbalist who knows the origin of his or her merchandise, or grow your own herbs to assure

optimum potency and shelf life.

干燥的散装草药很方便携带，因为它们的制备和应用方式有很大的多样性。除了用于各种草药制剂外，一

些干草药还可以直接撒在动物的食物上。一般来说，根的保存时间是干叶材料的两到三倍。但不要储存超

过一年内可用的草药，并确保将草药存放在密封容器中，避免阳光直射。无论采用何种正确的储存方法，

干燥的草药最终都会氧化并失去效力。一些草药在干燥后几天内就会失去大部分药用和营养价值。从诚

实、知识渊博、了解商品来源的草药师那里购买草药，或者自己种植草药，以确保最佳功效和保质期。

=== PAGE 47 ===
FRESH HERBS

新鲜的香草

Fresh herbs, clipped, dug, or plucked directly from a garden, are rich in nutrients and medicinal constituents.

Provided that their physical nature allows for the form of preparation you need, fresh herbs are without compare in

terms of medicinal potency. While most herbs are strong when used fresh, others require at least partial drying

before they impart their active components into a useful medium. Cascara sagrada (Rhamnus purshiana) bark is one

example. This herbal laxative is far too strong if used fresh and should be dried for at least a full year to mellow it

before use. It is also poorly water soluble when fresh, and until it dries it will not infuse adequately in water for a

good tea.

直接从花园里剪下来、挖出来或采摘的新鲜药草富含营养和药用成分。只要它们的物理性质允许您需要的

准备形式，新鲜草药的药效是无与伦比的。虽然大多数草药在新鲜使用时效果很强，但其他草药在将其活

性成分传递到有用的介质中之前至少需要部分干燥。 Cascara sagrada (Rhamnus purshiana) 树皮就是一个例

子。如果新鲜使用，这种草药泻药的药力太强，在使用前应干燥至少一整年以使其软化。新鲜时它的水溶

性也很差，在干燥之前它无法充分浸泡在水中以制成好茶。

=== PAGE 48 ===
HERB CAPSULES

草药胶囊

Because dogs and cats have short digestive tracts, encapsulated herbs tend to pass right through them. Even if they

don’t, you may find some difficulty in getting a large enough dose into your animal. In horses, sheep, llamas, goats,

and other herbivores, capsules work fine—but plan on feeding the animals dozens of them. In these animals, you are

often better off feeding the bulk herb or using an extract.

由于狗和猫的消化道较短，因此封装的草药往往会直接通过它们。即使他们不这样做，您也可能会发现很

难给您的动物注射足够大的剂量。对于马、绵羊、美洲驼、山羊和其他食草动物来说，胶囊效果很好，但

计划给这些动物喂食几十个胶囊。对于这些动物，通常最好喂散装草药或使用提取物。

=== PAGE 49 ===
ALCOHOL EXTRACTS, OR TINCTURES

酒精提取物或酊剂

With few exceptions, an alcohol tincture is by far the most versatile, strongest, and most readily usable form of herb

preparation. It can be administered orally; used in topical applications; diluted with water; or used as part of an eye,

hair, or skin rinse.

除少数例外，酒精酊剂是迄今为止最通用、最强效且最容易使用的草药制剂形式。可以口服；用于局部应

用；用水稀释；或用作眼睛、头发或皮肤冲洗液的一部分。

A tincture is prepared by soaking a measured quantity of fresh or dried herb in a certain proportion of alcohol and

water, using a specific formula for each herb. The alcohol serves as a solvent that breaks down the plant material and

releases the active ingredients into a liquid base called a menstruum. After two days to two weeks (depending on the

method used) the menstruum is then strained and pressed from the plant material (called the marc), to produce the

finished liquid product. Alcohol tinctures offer the advantages of maximum potency and unlimited shelf life

provided they are stored properly.

酊剂是通过将一定数量的新鲜或干燥草药浸泡在一定比例的酒精和水中，并使用每种草药的特定配方来

制备的。酒精充当溶剂，分解植物材料并将活性成分释放到称为溶剂的液体基质中。两天到两周后（取决

于所使用的方法），从植物材料（称为果渣）中过滤并压榨溶剂，以生产出液体成品。如果储存得当，酒

精酊剂具有最大效力和无限保质期的优点。

The concentrated liquid nature of tincture preparations allows for their quick and complete absorption into the

body, even in the short digestive tracts of dogs and cats. When kept in 1-ounce dropper bottles, they can be carried

anywhere and are easy to use. The biggest problem with alcohol tinctures is getting them into an animal. These

preparations are typically 30–70 percent grain alcohol, and while typical dosages do not present any alcohol-toxicity

problems, animals truly hate the way they taste.

酊剂的浓缩液体性质使其能够快速、完全地被体内吸收，甚至在狗和猫的短消化道中也是如此。当保存

在 1 盎司滴管瓶中时，它们可以随身携带并且易于使用。酒精酊剂的最大问题是让它们进入动物体内。这

些制剂通常含有 30-70% 的谷物酒精，虽然典型剂量不会出现任何酒精毒性问题，但动物确实讨厌它们的味

道。

To make an herb tincture from fresh herbs, add 1 part herb to 2 parts menstruum.

要使用新鲜药草制作药草酊剂，请将 1 份药草加入 2 份月经液中。

There are two basic methods for making tinctures: one is a process called percolation, the other, simpler method,

=== PAGE 50 ===
is called maceration. The percolation method entails using a specially designed, cone-shaped glass vessel. Herb

material is placed into the cone, then the menstruum is poured over it, left to stand for a short while, and eventually

allowed to trickle (or percolate) through the plant material and out a tube at the bottom end of the vessel.

制作酊剂有两种基本方法：一种是称为渗滤的过程，另一种更简单的方法称为浸渍。渗滤方法需要使用

专门设计的锥形玻璃容器。将草药材料放入锥体中，然后将溶剂倒在其上，静置一小会儿，最后让其滴流

（或渗透）通过植物材料并从容器底端的管子中流出。

Making herb tinctures by maceration takes more time, but it is much simpler and requires no specialized

equipment. To make a macerated tincture, herb material is placed into a glass jar, plastic container, or other

nonmetallic container. The menstruum is poured over the herb and the entire mixture is covered with an airtight lid

and allowed to soak for a period of two weeks. The menstruum is then strained from the plant material (the marc), to

produce the finished liquid product.

通过浸渍制作草药酊剂需要更多时间，但它要简单得多，不需要专门的设备。为了制作浸渍酊剂，将草

药材料放入玻璃罐、塑料容器或其他非金属容器中。将月经倒在草药上，将整个混合物盖上密封盖，浸泡

两周。然后从植物材料（果渣）中过滤出溶剂，生产出液体成品。

The proportions of alcohol and water needed to make an herb tincture vary according to the solubility of the herb

itself. Some herbs, such as milk thistle seed, require a high percentage of alcohol to extract optimum quantities of

active constituents from their cell structures. Other herbs, such as raspberry leaf, require little or no alcohol to

extract their useful compounds. Fortunately, knowing what percentage of alcohol you need is easy because these

determinations have already been done for you. Most of the formulas used in contemporary herbal practice are from

the U.S. Pharmacopoeia and other standard references that have been used in the pharmaceutical production of

simple herb extracts throughout most of the twentieth century. This information is still used by herbalists and

laboratories throughout the world and can be found in several books about herbs and herbalism.

制作草药酊剂所需的酒精和水的比例根据草药本身的溶解度而变化。一些草药，例如水飞蓟种子，需要

高比例的酒精才能从其细胞结构中提取最佳数量的活性成分。其他草药，例如覆盆子叶，只需要很少的酒

精或不需要酒精来提取有用的化合物。幸运的是，知道您需要多少酒精百分比很容易，因为这些确定已经

为您完成。当代草药实践中使用的大多数配方都来自美国药典和其他标准参考文献，这些参考文献在二十

世纪的大部分时间里一直用于简单草药提取物的制药生产。这些信息仍然被世界各地的草药师和实验室使

用，并且可以在几本有关草药和草药学的书籍中找到。

The amount of menstruum needed to extract the active constituents from a plant also varies. With most fresh

(undried) herbs, you will need a 1:2 ratio of herbs to menstruum. Most dried herb materials require a 1:5 ratio. This

means that to make a tincture from the fresh root of dandelion, you need one part of chopped herb material (by

weight) to two parts of menstruum (by liquid volume). For example, 16 ounces of fresh root must be covered with

32 fluid ounces of menstruum to make a tincture (and the menstruum must be at least 40 percent alcohol). If you are

using dried root, 16 ounces of dried root material will require 80 fluid ounces of menstruum to make a tincture.

Make sense? Don’t worry if it doesn’t; we’ll simplify in a moment. So how does one make a menstruum?

从植物中提取活性成分所需的溶媒量也各不相同。对于大多数新鲜（未干燥）的草药，您需要草药与月

经液的比例为 1:2。大多数干草药材料需要 1:5 的比例。这意味着，要用新鲜的蒲公英根制作酊剂，您需要

一份切碎的草药材料（按重量计）和两份月经液（按液体体积计）。例如，必须用 32 液体盎司的月经液覆

盖 16 盎司的新鲜根才能制成酊剂（并且月经液的酒精含量必须至少为 40%）。如果您使用干根，则 16 盎

司干根材料需要 80 液量盎司的溶剂来制作酊剂。合理？如果没有，也不必担心；我们稍后会简化。那么如

何来月经呢？

The most accurate and inexpensive way to make a menstruum is to buy pure grain alcohol (brand named

Everclear) at a liquor store. Everclear is 95 percent pure grain alcohol (190 proof). For simplicity, let’s just call it a

pure, 100 percent alcohol. To make a 70 percent alcohol menstruum, we would add 30 percent water to its volume

(i.e., add 3 parts water to 7 parts alcohol). If it’s a 50 percent menstruum we need, then all we have to do is add an

equal (50/50) amount of water. It’s that simple. Unfortunately, Everclear isn’t available in some portions of the U.S.,

so a medicine maker may have to do some liquor shopping. For tinctures that require 70 percent alcohol, uncut 151

proof rum works fine (it’s 75 percent alcohol). For a 50 percent menstruum, you can use 100 proof vodka (it’s 50

percent alcohol), and so forth.

配制月经最准确、最便宜的方法是在酒类商店购买纯谷物酒精（品牌名为 Everclear）。 Everclear 是 95%

的纯谷物酒精（190 度）。为简单起见，我们将其称为纯 100% 酒精。为了制备 70% 的酒精溶剂，我们需

=== PAGE 51 ===
要在其体积中添加 30% 的水（即，将 3 份水添加到 7 份酒精中）。如果我们需要 50% 的月经，那么我们所

要做的就是添加等量 (50/50) 的水。就是这么简单。不幸的是，Everclear 在美国某些地区不可用，因此制药

商可能不得不购买一些酒类。对于需要 70% 酒精度的酊剂，未切割的 151 度朗姆酒效果很好（酒精度为

75%）。对于 50% 的月经，您可以使用 100 度伏特加（酒精含量为 50%），等等。

Now here’s the simplified version of medicine making we promised. Get some fresh or dried herb, chop it up or

grind it as fine as possible, put it in a container, then add enough menstruum (of the appropriate strength) to just

barely cover the herb. Cover the container, then let it sit for two weeks, strain the mixture through a cloth, and store

the liquid in an airtight glass jar. Amber glass is best because it blocks ultraviolet rays that may damage your

tincture. You now have an herb tincture. The primary rule in this simplified method of making tincture is always to

use the correct percentage of alcohol in your menstruum. If you do, you will always end up with a nice tincture by

covering a maximum amount of chopped or ground herb with a minimum amount of menstruum.

现在这是我们承诺的制药的简化版本。取一些新鲜或干燥的草药，将其切碎或磨碎，尽可能细，放入容

器中，然后添加足够的月经剂（适当强度）以刚好覆盖草药。盖上容器，放置两周，用布过滤混合物，并

将液体储存在密封的玻璃罐中。琥珀色玻璃是最好的，因为它可以阻挡可能损坏酊剂的紫外线。你现在有

一种草药酊剂。这种制作酊剂的简化方法的主要规则始终是在月经中使用正确的酒精百分比。如果你这样

做，你总是会通过用最少量的月经覆盖最大量的切碎或磨碎的草药来获得美味的酊剂。

=== PAGE 52 ===
GLYCERIN-BASED HERB EXTRACTS, OR GLYCERITES

甘油基草药提取物或甘油酯

Glycerites are made essentially the same way as alcohol extracts, but a solution of 60 percent vegetable glycerin and

40 percent water is used in place of alcohol. The big advantage of glycerites in animal care is their palatability—

glycerin tastes sweet, with a flavor and consistency similar to light corn syrup. While some glycerin-based extracts

are not as potent as their alcohol counterparts, they allow pet owners to get the herbs into their animals in the first

place—hence, half the battle is won. Potency can then be adjusted by increasing the dosage. Vegetable glycerin is

refined from coconut oils, and despite its syrupy-sweet flavor, it is metabolized in a manner similar to that of

triglycerides, not sugar. This means it can be used safely in animals with alcohol sensitivity or in those with

diabetes. Glycerites do not keep indefinitely but remain viable for at least two years if refrigerated.

甘油的制备方法与酒精提取物基本相同，但使用 60% 植物甘油和 40% 水的溶液代替酒精。甘油在动物护理

中的一大优势是其适口性——甘油味道甜，其味道和稠度类似于淡玉米糖浆。虽然一些基于甘油的提取物

不如酒精提取物有效，但它们可以让宠物主人首先将草药摄入到他们的动物体内——因此，战斗就赢了一

半。然后可以通过增加剂量来调整效力。植物甘油是从椰子油中精炼而成的，尽管具有糖浆般的甜味，但

它的代谢方式类似于甘油三酯，而不是糖。这意味着它可以安全地用于对酒精敏感的动物或患有糖尿病的

动物。甘油不能无限期保存，但如果冷藏，至少可以保存两年。

The biggest disadvantages of glycerites are their limited shelf life (one to two years) and, in many cases, their

strength. Glycerin is not as strong a solvent as alcohol, and many herbs are not taken up well into a glycerin

menstruum, especially if they are of a resinous nature. However, some herbs, especially those that are highly water

soluble, release their active ingredients into glycerin very well. To find out if a particular herb that interests you is

good for making glycerites, refer to one or more of the books we recommend at the end of this section.

甘油的最大缺点是其保质期有限（一到两年），并且在许多情况下其强度也有限。甘油的溶剂强度不如

酒精，许多草药不能很好地被甘油溶剂吸收，特别是当它们具有树脂性质时。然而，一些草药，尤其是那

些高度水溶性的草药，可以很好地将其活性成分释放到甘油中。要了解您感兴趣的特定草药是否适合制作

甘油，请参阅本节末尾我们推荐的一本或多本书籍。

=== PAGE 53 ===
WATER INFUSIONS (HERB TEAS)

泡水（香草茶）

Infusions are made by steeping a specific quantity of plant material in hot water. The disadvantages of using teas

internally for animals are twofold: many animals don’t like tea, and it can be difficult to feed an animal enough tea

to bring about therapeutic results. Unlike tinctures, which provide a plant’s active constituents in a highly

concentrated, fully assimilable form, teas generally amount to a weaker medicine, and plant compounds that are not

water soluble are not imparted to the animal.

输液是将一定量的植物材料浸泡在热水中制成的。给动物喝茶有双重缺点：许多动物不喜欢茶，而且很难

给动物喂足够的茶来产生治疗效果。与酊剂不同的是，酊剂以高度浓缩、完全可吸收的形式提供植物活性

成分，茶通常是一种较弱的药物，并且不溶于水的植物化合物不会传递给动物。

Infusions are especially useful for skin and coat rinses and as vitamin- and mineral-rich tonic food supplements.

When mixed into an animal’s food, an herb tea provides most of what a dried or fresh herb offers in a form that is

quickly and more easily absorbed into the body. Herb teas also offer the advantage of melding with the flavor of an

animal’s diet without adding a new texture to the food—an important attribute for those who wish to feed nutritive

herbs to a finicky feline.

输液特别适用于皮肤和皮毛冲洗以及作为富含维生素和矿物质的滋补食品补充剂。当与动物食物混合

时，药草茶可以提供干燥或新鲜药草的大部分成分，并且更容易被人体快速吸收。药草茶还具有与动物饮

食的味道融合的优点，而不会给食物添加新的质地——对于那些希望给挑剔的猫科动物喂食营养药草的人

来说，这是一个重要的属性。

=== PAGE 54 ===
DECOCTIONS

汤剂

A decoction is an infusion that requires some gentle simmering to make a strong enough preparation for therapeutic

use. Decoction is required of many roots when the plant material is too insoluble in water to allow a strong enough

infusion. Decoctions should be prepared using a minimum of heat. Simmer the herb for about fifteen minutes at a

temperature that is only slightly above the boiling point. Too much heat destroys many of the plant constituents you

wish to employ. Decoctions are used in the same manner as water infusions, but they tend to be strong in

comparison.

汤剂是一种输液，需要温和地煮沸以制成足够浓的制剂用于治疗用途。当植物材料太难溶于水而无法进行

足够浓的浸剂时，需要对许多根进行煎煮。制备汤剂时应使用最少的热量。将药草在仅略高于沸点的温度

下煮约十五分钟。过多的热量会破坏许多您想要使用的植物成分。汤剂的使用方法与水输液相同，但相比

之下，汤剂往往更浓。

Completely cover the herb with olive oil to make an oil infusion.

用橄榄油完全覆盖药草，制成油浸剂。

=== PAGE 55 ===
Then cover the mixture and store for at least one month.

然后盖上混合物并保存至少一个月。

To make a poultice, mash the herb with water or vegetable oil until it forms a paste.

制作膏剂时，将草药与水或植物油一起捣碎，直至形成糊状。

=== PAGE 56 ===
Then you can apply the poultice directly to your animal’s skin or fur.

然后，您可以将药膏直接涂抹在动物的皮肤或毛皮上。

=== PAGE 57 ===
OIL INFUSIONS

输油

An oil infusion is produced by completely covering an herb with olive oil and allowing it to steep in a covered

nonmetallic container in a warm location for at least one month. The oil is then pressed out and stored in the

refrigerator for up to one year. Although several choices of oil can be used, olive oil possesses its own preservative

qualities, is relatively affordable, and is nourishing to the body, both internally and externally. Oil infusions are

excellent for topical applications, acting to soothe and protect the affected area while holding the herb constituents at

the site where they are applied. Extra caution should be used when applying oil to burns or infected areas because it

may seal in heat and bacteria.

油浸液是通过用橄榄油完全覆盖药草并将其在有盖的非金属容器中在温暖的地方浸泡至少一个月来制成

的。然后将油压出并在冰箱中保存长达一年。尽管可以使用多种油，但橄榄油具有其自身的防腐特性，价

格相对便宜，并且对身体有内在和外在的滋养作用。油浸液非常适合局部使用，可以舒缓和保护受影响的

区域，同时将草药成分保留在使用的部位。在烧伤或感染部位涂抹油时应格外小心，因为它可能会锁住热

量和细菌。

In these cases, make sure that the possibility of infection has been addressed with a good, clean antimicrobial

preparation and the burn has entirely cooled before anything is applied.

在这些情况下，请确保使用良好、干净的抗菌制剂解决了感染的可能性，并且在使用任何药物之前烧伤

部位已完全冷却。

=== PAGE 58 ===
POULTICES

膏药

A poultice is made by mashing plant material (usually dried foliage) with enough water or vegetable oil to make a

wet, pesto-like paste. Poultices are good in topical field applications when other preparations are impossible to

make. A simple poultice can be applied directly to an animal’s skin, or it can be made into a compress that can be

secured onto the animal. To make a compress, wrap the wet poultice in a piece of clean cloth, allowing the liquid to

freely soak through the cloth. Wrap the compress onto the affected body part and secure with knots.

膏药是通过将植物材料（通常是干燥的叶子）与足够的水或植物油捣碎制成湿的香蒜酱状糊状物而制成

的。当无法制备其他制剂时，膏剂在局部现场应用中效果很好。一种简单的药膏可以直接涂抹在动物的皮

肤上，也可以制成可以固定在动物身上的敷料。制作敷布时，将湿的膏药包裹在一块干净的布中，让液体

自由地渗透到布中。将敷料包裹在受影响的身体部位并用结固定。

To make a fomentation, secure a cloth over the affected area of skin and pour the infusion over it until the cloth

is soaked.

热敷时，将一块布固定在患处的皮肤上，然后将输液倒在上面，直到布浸湿。

=== PAGE 59 ===
SALVES AND OINTMENTS

药膏和药膏

Salves and ointments are simply thickened oil infusions. In making salves, beeswax is frequently used as the

thickening agent. The thinner ointment preparations typically employ coconut butter, particularly if the ointments

are to be used in suppository applications. The oil infusion is gently heated, and the beeswax or coconut butter is

melted into the liquid until the cooled product yields the consistency that is desired.

药膏和药膏只是稠化的油输液。在制作药膏时，蜂蜡经常被用作增稠剂。较稀的软膏制剂通常使用椰子

油，特别是当软膏用于栓剂应用时。将油浸液轻轻加热，将蜂蜡或椰子油融化到液体中，直到冷却的产品

达到所需的稠度。

For salves, use a ratio of 1 ounce of beeswax or cocoa butter to 8 ounces of oil. If the salve or ointment turns out

to be too thick or thin when it has cooled, gently reheat it and adjust the proportion of beeswax or cocoa butter.

Suppository molds and salve tins are available through herb catalogs and at some drugstores.

对于药膏，使用 1 盎司蜂蜡或可可脂与 8 盎司油的比例。如果冷却后发现药膏或软膏太厚或太薄，请轻

轻重新加热并调整蜂蜡或可可脂的比例。栓剂模具和药膏罐可通过草药目录和一些药店购买。

As with oil infusions, extra caution should be used when applying salves or ointments to areas of the body that are

burned or infected. In these cases, make sure that a good, clean antimicrobial preparation is used and that the burn

has cooled completely before applying any kind of topical treatment to the area.

与输油一样，在身体烧伤或感染的部位使用药膏或药膏时应格外小心。在这些情况下，请确保使用良

好、干净的抗菌制剂，并且在对烧伤区域进行任何局部治疗之前，烧伤部位已完全冷却。

=== PAGE 60 ===
FOMENTATIONS

热敷

A fomentation is used for topical applications where a water or oil infusion must remain on a particular body site for

a specific period. Gauze or another cloth material is placed over the area, and the infusion is poured onto the

dressing until it is soaked. Mustard packs, castor oil packs, and other traditional remedies employ this method. This

is a good approach for horses with fungal infections of the skin or other animals who don’t mind “wearing” an

herbal ornament for a while.

热敷用于局部应用，其中水或油输液必须在特定的身体部位保留特定的时间。将纱布或其他布材料放在该

区域上，并将输液倒在敷料上直至浸透。芥末包、蓖麻油包和其他传统疗法都采用这种方法。对于患有皮

肤真菌感染的马或其他不介意“佩戴”草药装饰品一段时间的动物来说，这是一个好方法。

=== PAGE 61 ===
STANDARDIZED EXTRACTS

标准化提取物

A standardized extract is more of a plant drug than an herbal medicine. These preparations are made by scientifically

increasing the content of certain active ingredients in order to bring about specific therapeutic effects. This is done

by removing a desired active ingredient from the chemistry of a particular plant species, then adding it back to the

extract at much higher concentration. For example, in nature, milk thistle seeds contain anywhere from 2 percent to

6 percent silymarin, the most medicinally active component of the plant. In cases of severe liver damage or toxicity,

a much higher percentage of silymarin may be needed to quickly bring about a therapeutic effect. A milk thistle

extract that has been “standardized” to as much as 80 percent silymarin can be used in such cases.

标准化提取物更像是植物药物而不是草药。这些制剂是通过科学增加某些活性成分的含量而制成的，以产

生特定的治疗效果。这是通过从特定植物物种的化学成分中去除所需的活性成分，然后以更高的浓度将其

添加回提取物中来完成的。例如，在自然界中，水飞蓟种子含有 2% 至 6% 的水飞蓟素，这是植物中最具药

用活性的成分。在严重肝损伤或毒性的情况下，可能需要更高比例的水飞蓟素才能快速产生治疗效果。在

这种情况下，可以使用水飞蓟素含量已“标准化”至 80% 的水飞蓟提取物。

On the surface, standardized extracts may seem like a superior form of herbal medicine. In the aforementioned

example in which milk thistle is indicated, this is absolutely true. However, it’s important to remember that when we

standardize an herb we alter its physical and energetic nature. Our manipulation of its nature is based on our

scientific understanding of only one or a few of its chemical components. In its natural form, each herb is composed

of hundreds of chemical components that are arranged in a unique, synergistic manner that cannot be replicated by

science. It is this synergy that makes herbs a mysteriously effective form of medicine. Every time that we alter the

chemistry of an herb, we change everything that the herb represents in terms of a natural and holistic medicine. To

the holistic herbalist, the question is not so much what can be gained by standardizing an herb but rather how much

is lost in the process.

从表面上看，标准化提取物似乎是一种高级形式的草药。在上述提到水飞蓟的例子中，这是绝对正确

的。然而，重要的是要记住，当我们标准化一种草药时，我们改变了它的物理和能量性质。我们对其性质

的操纵是基于我们对其一种或几种化学成分的科学理解。在其天然形式下，每种草药都由数百种化学成分

组成，这些化学成分以独特的协同方式排列，无法通过科学复制。正是这种协同作用使草药成为一种神秘

有效的药物形式。每当我们改变一种草药的化学成分时，我们就改变了该草药在天然和整体医学方面所代

表的一切。对于整体草药医生来说，问题不在于通过标准化草药可以获得什么，而在于在此过程中损失了

多少。

The bottom line is that standardized extracts are best reserved only for specific indications—they do not represent

a complete form of herbal medicine.

最重要的是，标准化提取物最好只用于特定的适应症——它们并不代表草药的完整形式。

=== PAGE 62 ===
THE CONNECTION BETWEEN HERBS AND DIET

草药和饮食之间的联系

To use herbs to the best of their potential, we must take on a holistic perspective of health and healing that views all

components of mind, body, spirit, and environment as equal parts of an individual’s well-being. At the core of this

“whole body” perspective is a good diet. Without balanced nutrition, the use of herbal medicines in the holistic care

of your animal is a waste of time, money, and plants.

为了充分发挥草药的潜力，我们必须采取健康和治疗的整体视角，将思想、身体、精神和环境的所有组成

部分视为个人福祉的平等组成部分。这种“全身”观点的核心是良好的饮食。如果营养不均衡，使用草药对

动物进行全面护理就会浪费时间、金钱和植物。

The food that your animal eats should provide all of the nutritional components that are necessary for all organs

and systems of a healthy body to perform in harmonious unison. A properly functioning body does an amazing job

of preventing disease and healing itself, and to do this it requires the energies and nutrients of a well-balanced diet.

However, sometimes the body needs special measures of outside support to optimize its healing efforts to assist the

body at working harder, faster, longer, or more efficiently toward reestablishing a balanced state of holistic health.

Enter herbs.

动物吃的食物应提供健康身体的所有器官和系统和谐一致运转所需的所有营养成分。一个功能正常的身

体在预防疾病和自我治愈方面有着惊人的作用，而要做到这一点，需要均衡饮食的能量和营养。然而，有

时身体需要特殊的外部支持措施来优化其治疗效果，帮助身体更努力、更快、更长时间或更有效地恢复整

体健康的平衡状态。输入草药。

complement his diet with foodlike concentrations of fully assimilable protein, vitamin C, B complex

=== PAGE 63 ===
(including B12), vitamin A (beta-carotene), vitamin E, vitamin K, iron, potassium, calcium, phosphorus,

该配方奶粉可以每天每磅食物 1 茶匙的比例喂食（猫每天 ½ 茶匙），作为自然饮食的辅助品。虽然

它可能无法满足动物的所有补充营养需求，但它可以用食物般浓度的完全同化蛋白质、维生素 C、B
