In the holistic context in which they are used most effectively, herbs serve as functional adjuncts to good nutrition

by helping the body to use its innate and acquired resources more effectively. For example, echinacea does not act as

a substitute for the body’s immune system but serves to stimulate the body’s natural defenses into working harder,

thus boosting the body’s abilities to resist infection. Likewise, herbs such as dandelion root, Oregon grape, and

burdock assist in the elimination of waste from the body by stimulating the liver and gallbladder into working more

efficiently. These supportive functions are diet dependent: in order for an herb to call upon the body to do something

extraordinary, there must be an adequate store of energy and building materials with which the body can work.

在最有效使用的整体背景下，草药可以作为良好营养的功能性辅助剂，帮助身体更有效地利用其先天和

获得的资源。例如，紫锥菊并不能替代人体的免疫系统，而是可以刺激人体的自然防御系统更加努力地工

作，从而增强人体抵抗感染的能力。同样，蒲公英根、俄勒冈葡萄和牛蒡等草药可以刺激肝脏和胆囊更有

效地工作，从而帮助消除体内废物。这些支持功能依赖于饮食：为了让草药能够号召身体做一些非凡的事

情，必须有足够的能量和建筑材料来供身体工作。

=== PAGE 64 ===
Many people use herbs only for treating the symptoms of a disease in the absence of adequate nutrition and

without considering the whole being. For instance, if we use an herbal ear oil externally to treat a chronic ear

infection without addressing why the body is unable to fight the infection by itself, we are not using a holistic

approach toward healing. Instead, we are treating only the symptoms of a disorder that emanates from the body’s

inability to defend itself. While the ear oil may inhibit the external microbial cause of the infection, it is really doing

nothing more than serving as a natural alternative to any number of pharmaceutical preparations that may be able to

alleviate symptoms more quickly. However, if our goals are to reach beyond the symptoms to affect the underlying

causes of disease, the healing effort must begin by ensuring that the body is afforded everything it needs to heal

itself. In other words, we must provide the body with the foundation of holistic health—complete nutrition—before

our healing efforts with herbal medicines can begin to approach curative results.

许多人使用草药只是为了治疗疾病的症状，缺乏足够的营养，没有考虑整体。例如，如果我们在外部使

用草药耳油来治疗慢性耳部感染，而不解决为什么身体无法自行抵抗感染的原因，那么我们就没有使用整

体治疗方法。相反，我们只治疗因身体无法自我防御而产生的疾病症状。虽然耳油可以抑制感染的外部微

生物，但它实际上只不过是作为许多药物制剂的天然替代品，可以更快地缓解症状。然而，如果我们的目

标是超越症状，影响疾病的根本原因，那么治疗工作就必须从确保身体获得自我治愈所需的一切开始。换

句话说，我们必须为身体提供整体健康的基础——完整的营养——然后我们的草药治疗才能开始达到治疗

效果。

=== PAGE 65 ===
USING NUTRITIVE HERBS AS DIETARY SUPPLEMENTS

使用营养草药作为膳食补充剂

Many herbs are foods, and some provide nutritional qualities in such abundance that they can be used as nutritional

medicines or dietary supplements. Herbs provide minerals, vitamins, fatty acids, and other nutritional components in

a form that a body can fully utilize without becoming burdened with excess. Dandelion leaves, for instance, contain

impressive amounts of potassium and iron but not so much as to present a risk of toxicity. With nutritive herbs, the

body is given the chance to take the nutrients it needs and easily eliminate what it does not, unlike many highly

concentrated vitamin supplements that force the liver, kidneys, and digestive tract to work overtime at their jobs of

eliminating the excess. On the other hand, the nutritional content of herbs may vary considerably from plant to plant,

and in therapeutic or dietary situations where high concentrations of specific vitamins or minerals must be

guaranteed, herbs usually prove to be inadequate.

许多草药都是食物，有些草药提供的营养品质非常丰富，可以用作营养药物或膳食补充剂。草药以人体可

以充分利用的形式提供矿物质、维生素、脂肪酸和其他营养成分，而不会造成过量负担。例如，蒲公英叶

含有大量的钾和铁，但含量还没有达到中毒的风险。有了营养草药，身体就有机会获取所需的营养物质，

并轻松消除不需要的营养物质，这与许多高浓缩维生素补充剂不同，这些维生素补充剂迫使肝脏、肾脏和

消化道加班加点地工作，以消除多余的营养物质。 。另一方面，草本植物的营养成分可能因植物而异，在

必须保证高浓度的特定维生素或矿物质的治疗或饮食情况下，草本植物通常被证明是不够的。

Many herbs can be used as nutritional adjuncts to a good diet. Finding which nutritive herbs are best for the needs

of an individual animal comes from the one-on-one experience of the caregiver with his or her animal, but a simple

dried herb formula that can be used for most dogs, cats, horses, ferrets, and other animals can be found in the box on

page 38.

许多草药可以用作良好饮食的营养辅助剂。寻找最适合单个动物需求的营养草药来自于护理人员与他或

她的动物的一对一经验，但简单的干草药配方可用于大多数狗、猫、马、雪貂，以及其他动物可以在第 38

页的盒子中找到。

=== PAGE 66 ===
THE ETHICAL USE OF HERBS

草药的合乎道德的使用

We are living in a time when millions of people are turning away from anything they perceive as artificial,

unhealthy, or forced upon them. A huge natural health care industry has arisen, fueled by people who are eager to

embrace products, healing methods, and lifestyles that offer a healing step back toward nature. On the surface of this

“green revolution,” more people are becoming aware of the curative possibilities that exist beneath the trees, and a

renewed sense of hope for a healthy environment has been born. But in many ways, this scenario also brings about a

whole new level of environmental crisis. While a great deal of promise may exist in our growing awareness of

earth’s natural treasures, our journey toward “getting back to basics” is consuming resources faster than we can

learn to replace them. It seems that a great many of us have become so intoxicated by the freedom-based premise of

using selfprescribed natural alternatives, we have forgotten where they come from.

我们生活在这样一个时代，数百万人正在远离任何他们认为是人造的、不健康的或强加给他们的东西。在

人们渴望拥抱回归自然的产品、治疗方法和生活方式的推动下，一个巨大的天然保健行业已经兴起。在这

场“绿色革命”的表面上，越来越多的人开始意识到树下存在的治疗可能性，并且对健康环境的新希望已经

诞生。但从很多方面来说，这种情况也带来了全新水平的环境危机。尽管我们对地球自然宝藏的认识不断

增强，可能存在很大的希望，但我们“回归基础”的旅程正在消耗资源，而我们无法学会更换它们。似乎我

们中的许多人已经对使用自我规定的自然替代品的自由前提如此陶醉，我们已经忘记了它们来自哪里。

BASIC ETHICAL GUIDELINES FOR THE HARVESTING OF WILD

PLANTS

野生植物采收的基本道德准则

Follow these ethical guidelines if you wish to have the least impact on our earth while harvesting medicinal

plants from wild areas.

如果您希望在从野生地区收获药用植物时对我们的地球影响最小，请遵循这些道德准则。

• Never gather endangered or environmentally sensitive species. Many plants are abundant in certain

areas but relatively rare in others. Learn to recognize and use plant species in your home bioregion

that are abundant and resilient to human impact, while taking into account that the ecological niche

you see is a small, unique part of a much larger environmental picture. Get to know the general status

of the plants you are interested in from a global perspective. You may find that as an “ecoherbalist,”

your role among certain plants around your home is strictly that of guardian.

• 切勿采集濒临灭绝或环境敏感的物种。许多植物在某些地区丰富，但在其他地区则相对稀少。

学习识别和使用您的家乡生物区中丰富且能够抵御人类影响的植物物种，同时考虑到您看到

的生态位只是更大环境图景中一个小的、独特的部分。从全球角度了解您感兴趣的植物的总

体状况。您可能会发现，作为一名“生态草药师”，您在家里的某些植物中的角色严格来说是

守护者。

• Be absolutely certain of plant identification before you harvest. Gathering the wrong plants not only

may be harmful to you and your pets but may be wasteful and potentially damaging to the ecosystem

as well.

• 收获前要绝对确定植物的身份。采集错误的植物不仅可能对您和您的宠物有害，而且可能造成

浪费，并可能对生态系统造成破坏。

• Collect a small amount of plant material from several different stands to minimize your impact. Never

gather so much from a stand of plants that you can see a difference after your harvest. Remember,

mathematical solutions to the number of plants that can be ethically harvested do not apply in the

natural realm. The only way to determine how much is ethically acceptable is to begin learning about

=== PAGE 67 ===
the ecology of your bioregion before you harvest. Observe your impact over a long period of time,

and always gather conservatively.

• 从几个不同的展台收集少量植物材料，以尽量减少影响。切勿从一堆植物中采集过多的植物，

以免收获后您可以看到差异。请记住，可以合乎道德地收获的植物数量的数学解决方案不适

用于自然领域。确定多少在道德上可接受的唯一方法是在收获之前开始了解您的生物区域的

生态。长期观察你的影响，并始终保守地聚集。

• Never gather from a group of plants until you have thoroughly investigated the health, welfare,

sustainability, and interdependent elements of the entire area. Is there a healthier stand nearby? Is the

stand large enough to sustain your impact? Do you know the ecosystem well enough to harvest plants

in a manner that is conducive to its health? What may seem to be a lush, healthy stand of plants may

in fact be a biocommunity in trouble. Walk, look, listen, feel, and, most important, learn as much as

you can about the ways of the land before you begin your harvest.

• 在彻底调查整个区域的健康、福利、可持续性和相互依存要素之前，切勿从一组植物中采集。

附近有更健康的摊位吗？展台足够大以承受您的影响吗？您是否足够了解生态系统，能够以

有利于其健康的方式收获植物？看似茂盛、健康的植物群落实际上可能是陷入困境的生物群

落。走路、看、听、感觉，最重要的是，在开始收获之前，尽可能多地了解这片土地的情

况。

• Never gather more than you can conservatively use, bearing in mind that many herbs lose their

potency quickly after harvest. Unless you plan to make alcohol tinctures, expect no more than six

months to a year of shelf life for properly dried and stored herbs.

• 切勿采集超出您保守使用范围的草药，请记住，许多草药在收获后很快就会失去效力。除非您

打算制作酒精酊剂，否则正确干燥和储存的草药的保质期不会超过六个月到一年。

• Always ask permission before entering private lands, even if you are doing the landowner a favor by

pulling a few weeds. Check with your local land management agencies for permit requirements

before you begin gathering herbs from public lands.

• 在进入私人土地之前一定要征得许可，即使您拔掉一些杂草是在帮土地所有者一个忙。在开始

从公共土地上采集药草之前，请咨询当地的土地管理机构以了解许可证要求。

• Keep a journal of your observations during each visit to a harvest site and learn to work within

nature’s capacity. Remember, you will always be a student in nature, and there are no absolutes in

how an ecosystem operates. Maintain a set of wildcrafting site records, and keep a detailed log for

each wildcrafting venture. From these records, you can monitor your long-term impacts while

enriching your awareness of nature.

• 记录每次访问收获地点时的观察结果，并学会在大自然的能力范围内工作。请记住，您在大自

然中永远是一名学生，生态系统的运作方式没有绝对性。维护一套野生制作现场记录，并为

每个野生制作企业保留详细的日志。通过这些记录，您可以监控您的长期影响，同时丰富您

对自然的认识。

• Gather only from areas that are endemic to the plants you are looking for. Learn the typical elevation,

habitat, soil composition, exposure, and climatic requirements of each plant you wish to harvest, then

harvest from areas that match these criteria. Small, isolated stands of plants that have adapted to an

unusual set of environmental circumstances are particularly vulnerable to human impact and should

be used for learning, not for medicine making.

• 仅从您要寻找的植物特有的地区采集。了解您想要收获的每种植物的典型海拔、栖息地、土壤

成分、暴露程度和气候要求，然后从符合这些标准的地区进行收获。适应了不寻常环境条件

的小型、孤立的植物群特别容易受到人类的影响，应该用于学习，而不是用于制药。

• Learn the environmental issues of your area, and familiarize yourself with other people who have an

interest in the wild lands you will be working within, including other herbalists, the logging and

mining communities, developers, environmentalist groups, and government agencies. Learn about

their plans for the land, and adjust your activities. Plan ahead for the possibility of future impact.

• 了解您所在地区的环境问题，并熟悉对您将要工作的荒地感兴趣的其他人，包括其他草药师、

=== PAGE 68 ===
伐木和采矿社区、开发商、环保团体和政府机构。了解他们的土地计划，并调整您的活动。

提前计划未来影响的可能性。

• Find opportunities to salvage or transplant useful plants from areas that are scheduled to be heavily

impacted by human activities such as areas where trail or road construction is planned. Many areas

have ongoing native plant restoration projects under way. In these instances, you might be able to

assist with the survival of native species by “weeding out” the invasive, nonnative species.

• 寻找机会从计划受到人类活动严重影响的地区（例如计划建设步道或道路的地区）抢救或移植

有用植物。许多地区正在进行本土植物恢复项目。在这些情况下，您也许可以通过“清除”入

侵的非本地物种来帮助本地物种的生存。

• Find ideal stands that are representative of how a plant community should look, then don’t harvest

from them. Instead, preserve them for use as models from which to base your observations and

stewardship efforts at the sites from which you will be harvesting.

• 找到能够代表植物群落外观的理想林分，然后不要从中采摘。相反，请将它们保存为模型，作

为您在将要采伐的地点进行观察和管理工作的基础。

• Always use the correct tools and wear the right clothing to get your job done. Digging long taproots

from a steep, rocky hillside with a soupspoon while wearing penny loafers will result not only in

physical trauma to the herbalist but will tear apart the hillside as well. Be considerate of the

environment by acknowledging that the human body is poorly adapted to many of the tasks we

perform there.

• 始终使用正确的工具并穿着正确的衣服来完成工作。穿着便士乐福鞋，用汤匙从陡峭的岩石山

坡上挖长的主根，不仅会对草药师造成身体伤害，还会撕裂山坡。通过承认人体不太适应我

们在那里执行的许多任务来考虑环境。

• Never gather from stands that are wilted or otherwise unhealthy. Not only may sick plants have altered

chemistries but they may be covered with poison as well. Contact your county, state, or federal weed

abatement officials and learn about weed control programs in your area before you harvest anything.

Check your local noxious weed list, and see if there is an opportunity to reduce the distribution of

toxic herbicides by offering to hand-pull the plants for healing purposes. Many homeowners and

farmers will welcome you onto their land to gather plants such as dandelion, Saint-John’s-wort,

mullein, burdock, or countless others. By focusing your wildcrafting efforts toward plants that people

generally hate, you will be giving a precious gift of healing back to the environment by reducing the

use of toxic herbicides.

• 切勿在枯萎或其他不健康的摊位上采集。生病的植物不仅可能改变化学成分，而且还可能被毒

物覆盖。在收获任何东西之前，请联系您所在的县、州或联邦除草官员，了解您所在地区的

杂草控制计划。检查当地的有毒杂草清单，看看是否有机会通过手拉植物进行治疗来减少有

毒除草剂的分布。许多房主和农民都会欢迎您来到他们的土地上采集蒲公英、圣约翰草、毛

蕊花、牛蒡或无数其他植物。通过将你的野生制作工作集中在人们普遍讨厌的植物上，你将

通过减少有毒除草剂的使用来给环境带来治愈的宝贵礼物。

• Be as quiet as possible and plan every step when you enter a wild area. Stop frequently to look, listen,

and feel the earth; and don’t forget to look behind you to monitor the impact you may be causing

while en route to that special patch.

• 进入野外区域时，尽可能保持安静并计划好每一步。经常停下来观察、聆听和感受地球；并且

不要忘记回头看看你在前往那个特殊补丁的途中可能造成的影响。

• When gathering from a stand of plants, work at a deliberate pace that allows you to remain conscious

of your surroundings and of the task at hand. Harvest carefully and thoughtfully. Don’t attack the

plants; work as the loving caretaker you are.

• 当从植物丛中采集时，请以从容的节奏工作，这样您就可以保持对周围环境和手头任务的意

识。仔细、深思熟虑地收获。不要攻击植物；作为一个充满爱心的看护者。

• Always be careful to use the proper processing and storage methods for the herbs you gather. Spoilage

equates to waste—one of the worst types of vicarious human impact. Good wildcrafting ethics are not

=== PAGE 69 ===
exclusive to your time in the field—take care of the plants all the way from earth to medicine.

• 始终小心地对您采集的草药使用正确的加工和储存方法。腐败就等于浪费——这是人类间接影

响最严重的类型之一。良好的野生制作道德并不局限于您在野外的时间——从地球到医学的

整个过程中都要照顾好植物。

• Stay obscure during your harvest and field studies. If you attract uninvited attention to a stand of

plants, the result might be added impact from curious onlookers. A good rule is to always focus your

efforts in areas where you will remain out of the view of other people.

• 在收获和田间研究期间保持低调。如果你的植物群吸引了不请自来的注意，结果可能会增加好

奇旁观者的影响。一条好的规则是始终将精力集中在别人看不到的领域。

• Be critical of your human shortcomings. We are foreigners in wild areas. Strive to deepen your

awareness to understand that even the simplest organisms of nature serve complex roles in the

environment, and that we are all just beginning to learn the ways of the wild. Nothing is insignificant,

and virtually every organism in an ecosystem is interdependent with the plants we harvest.

• 批评你的人性缺点。我们是荒野里的外国人。努力加深你的认识，了解即使是最简单的自然有

机体在环境中也发挥着复杂的作用，而我们都刚刚开始学习野外生存方式。没有什么是微不

足道的，几乎生态系统中的每个生物体都与我们收获的植物相互依存。

• Never reseed a stand of plants to an extent that exceeds the natural density that existed prior to your

harvest. A human-engineered overpopulation of plants can be as devastating to an ecosystem as

careless overharvesting. Watch the bioregion from which you are harvesting over a period of several

years, and take note of how each species reseeds itself. Then try to replicate what nature would do in

your absence. Many plants compete with one another. Propagating an overabundance of a species

may be satisfactory to our conscience but may also pass a death sentence to dozens of noncompeting

plants and interdependent organisms.

• 重新播种植物时，切勿使其超过收获前的自然密度。人为造成的植物数量过多对生态系统的破

坏性可能与粗心的过度采伐一样严重。观察您在几年内收获的生物区域，并记下每个物种如

何重新播种。然后尝试复制你不在时大自然会发生的事情。许多植物相互竞争。过度繁殖一

个物种可能会让我们的良心满意，但也可能对数十种非竞争植物和相互依存的生物体宣判死

刑。

• Accept your personal weaknesses, identify your chronic mistakes, then add to this list your own

personal set of wildcrafting guidelines.

• 接受你的个人弱点，找出你长期犯的错误，然后将你自己的一套野生制作指南添加到此列表

中。

To learn more about the earth-conscious harvest, use, and preservation of wild medicinal plants, pick up a

copy of From Earth to Herbalist by Gregory L. Tilford (Mountain Press Publishing, 1998).

要了解有关野生药用植物的环保收获、使用和保存的更多信息，请阅读 Gregory L. Tilford 所著的

《从地球到草药师》（Mountain Press Publishing，1998 年）。

Many plant species are disappearing not so much because they are overharvested but because they are

misrepresented in the marketplace. Goldenseal (Hydrastis canadensis), for example, has been one of the most

popular North American herbs of commerce for centuries, but it is also one of the most misused. Like many other

herbs, goldenseal continues to be heralded as some sort of miracle medicine that is effective against virtually any

microbe that terrifies us enough to try something “alternative.” Indeed, the popularity of this and many other herbs

has arisen from therapeutic success stories and promising scientific studies, but most of their appeal is attributable to

marketing savvy and no small measure of consumer hysteria. In truth, most plant medicines work within narrow

parameters of therapeutic usefulness. Goldenseal is not a systemic antibiotic that courses through the body to fight

infection like a shot of penicillin; instead, it works only to inhibit microbes it comes in direct contact with on the

surface membranes of the digestive tract, eyes, and nasal passages.

许多植物物种正在消失，与其说是因为它们被过度采伐，不如说是因为它们在市场上被歪曲了。例如，

加拿大白毛茛（Hydrastis canadensis）几个世纪以来一直是北美最受欢迎的商业草药之一，但它也是最被滥

用的草药之一。与许多其他草药一样，白毛茛仍然被誉为某种神奇药物，几乎可以有效对抗任何让我们害

=== PAGE 70 ===
怕尝试“替代品”的微生物。事实上，这种草药和许多其他草药的流行源于治疗的成功故事和有前景的科学

研究，但它们的吸引力大部分归因于营销精明和消费者的歇斯底里。事实上，大多数植物药物的治疗作用

范围很窄。白毛茛并不是一种像注射青霉素那样在体内循环以对抗感染的全身性抗生素。相反，它仅能抑

制与其直接接触的消化道、眼睛和鼻道表面膜上的微生物。

We must also take into account that many medicinal plants are at risk of disappearing because of factors totally

unrelated to their uses as medicines. Pipsissewa (Chimaphila spp.), for instance, is used as a “secret ingredient” in

certain brands of soft drinks, and the habitat destruction associated with its harvest may be more devastating than the

loss of the plants themselves. Another example is goldthread (Coptis spp.), which is an old-growth forest inhabitant

that is quickly running out of places to live in the Pacific Northwest. Goldthread is not a popular plant of commerce

in North America, but the old-growth firs and cedars it lives beneath are.

我们还必须考虑到，许多药用植物由于与其药物用途完全无关的因素而面临消失的风险。例如，

Pipsissewa（Chimaphila spp.）被用作某些品牌软饮料的“秘密成分”，其收获带来的栖息地破坏可能比植物

本身的损失更具破坏性。另一个例子是黄连（Coptis spp.），它是一种古老的森林居民，在太平洋西北部很

快就没有地方居住了。金丝在北美并不是一种受欢迎的商业植物，但它生长的老冷杉和雪松却是。

And then there’s all the hype. Newsstands are packed with the latest word about scientific herbal breakthroughs,

even about the same medicines that just yesterday were considered “snake oil” in the eyes of science. Some herbs

are becoming as fashionable as the fastest computer: if you haven’t tried the latest herbal craze, then your life is

unnecessarily difficult. Don’t take Prozac—we’ve got Saint-John’s-wort, the herbal alternative for chronic

depression. Too busy to slow down? Don’t worry. The latest double-blind studies say that we can boost the body’s

immune system with echinacea, cat’s claw, astragalus, and ginseng.

然后就是所有的炒作。报摊上充斥着有关科学草药突破的最新消息，甚至包括昨天在科学界被认为是“蛇

油”的药物。有些草药正变得像最快的计算机一样流行：如果你还没有尝试过最新的草药热潮，那么你的生

活就不必要地困难了。不要服用百忧解——我们有圣约翰草，这是治疗慢性抑郁症的草药替代品。太忙没

时间放慢脚步？不用担心。最新的双盲研究表明，我们可以通过紫锥花、猫爪草、黄芪和人参来增强人体

的免疫系统。

Herbs are touching the far reaches of our society at an unprecedented rate. Much of what drives this green

revolution is born from solid scientific discovery and consumers’ independent desire to take charge of their health

and well-being. Certainly, these are good goals, but where do herbs come from? Is there something we should know

about their natural environment? What do these plants contribute to their ecosystems? Do they really work the way

that we are led to believe? What makes herbs different from conventional medicines? What effect is our

consumption having upon plant populations and their environments?

草药正以前所未有的速度触及我们社会的各个角落。推动这场绿色革命的动力很大程度上源于扎实的科

学发现和消费者掌控自己健康和福祉的独立愿望。当然，这些都是很好的目标，但是草药从哪里来呢？关

于他们的自然环境，我们有什么应该了解的吗？这些植物对其生态系统有何贡献？它们真的按照我们所相

信的方式工作吗？草药与传统药物有何不同？我们的消费对植物种群及其环境有何影响？

=== PAGE 71 ===
Our point is this: We have to be careful. If we wish to use and sustain our botanical resources into the future, we

must step away from all the hoopla long enough to find healthful solutions for the plants themselves. The answers to

all of the above questions rest within our willingness to look beyond the sensational advertising to see what herbs

really are and what they represent in the larger global scheme of things. Until we do, our herbal heritage will

continue to disappear under the pressures of ignorance, waste, and greed.

我们的观点是：我们必须小心。如果我们希望在未来使用和维持我们的植物资源，我们必须远离所有喧

嚣，为植物本身找到健康的解决方案。上述所有问题的答案取决于我们愿意超越耸人听闻的广告，看看草

药到底是什么以及它们在更大的全球计划中代表什么。在此之前，我们的草药遗产将在无知、浪费和贪婪

的压力下继续消失。

Many North American medicinal plants of commerce are now being cultivated, but sadly, many of them continue

to disappear from the wild. While part of the problem stems from unethical wildcrafting practices, the demise for

plants such as goldenseal and American ginseng originates from a complexity of economic and environmental

causes. As herbalists, we could easily point an accusatory finger at the herb industry, but this would not be fair.

Many herbalists have chosen to exclude wild plants such as goldenseal, American ginseng, black cohosh, and osha

from their personal medicine cabinets as a gesture, if not a preventive measure against their demise. But in sad

reality, such measures provide only a bandage treatment for a global problem. The painful truth is that too many

people are impacting too much of the planet for too many reasons. Indeed, consumer demands are taking a serious

toll on plants such as goldenseal and American ginseng, but these and thousands of other plant species are also

disappearing under the combined pressures of logging, grazing, mining, weed abatement, urban development,

farming, pollution, recreational impact, and several other human-centered factors.

许多北美商业药用植物现在正在种植，但遗憾的是，其中许多继续从野外消失。虽然部分问题源于不道

德的野生加工行为，但金毛草和西洋参等植物的消亡却源于复杂的经济和环境原因。作为草药医生，我们

可以轻易地指责草药行业，但这并不公平。许多草药师选择将白毛茛、西洋参、黑升麻和奥莎等野生植物

排除在个人药柜之外，这即使不是预防它们死亡的预防措施，也是一种姿态。但在悲惨的现实中，这些措

施只能为全球性问题提供绷带治疗。令人痛苦的事实是，太多的人由于太多的原因而影响着地球的太多地

=== PAGE 72 ===
区。事实上，消费者的需求正在对金毛草和西洋参等植物造成严重影响，但在伐木、放牧、采矿、除草、

城市发展、农业、污染、娱乐影响以及其他一些以人为本的因素。

So then, what can we do to save medicinal plants? On a community level, we can share what we learn from books

such as this one by educating others on the curative possibilities that may exist beneath the trees around their homes.

Show your neighbor a medicinal plant that grows on the roadside—such as mullein, dandelion, licorice, Saint-

John’s-wort, or milkweed—and raise the question of whether a weed is really just a weed. Tell people about the

plight of goldenseal, and remind them that the greatest curative gifts of this plant may yet to be discovered. Then tell

them they can use Oregon grape as a substitute.

那么，我们该如何拯救药用植物呢？在社区层面，我们可以通过教育其他人了解他们家周围的树下可能

存在的治疗可能性，来分享我们从这本书中学到的知识。向你的邻居展示路边生长的药用植物，例如毛蕊

花、蒲公英、甘草、圣约翰草或马利筋，并提出这样的问题：杂草是否真的只是杂草。告诉人们白毛茛的

困境，并提醒他们这种植物最伟大的治疗天赋可能尚未被发现。然后告诉他们可以使用俄勒冈葡萄作为替

代品。

On a personal level, you can accomplish even more. Join organizations such as United Plant Savers, become

involved with native plant clubs in your area, or become actively involved in land restoration efforts. If you use

herbs, learn as much as you can about the plants and the ecosystems they live in.

在个人层面上，您可以取得更多成就。加入联合植物保护者等组织，加入您所在地区的本土植物俱乐

部，或积极参与土地恢复工作。如果您使用草药，请尽可能多地了解植物及其生存的生态系统。

Above all, take time to evaluate and improve yourself as a consumer of our planet’s resources, and learn how to

give something back for everything you consume.

最重要的是，作为地球资源的消费者，花时间评估和提高自己，并学习如何回馈你所消耗的一切。

AN A-Z GUIDE TO HERBS FOR ANIMALS

动物草药 A-Z 指南

Chapter 2

第2章

Materia Medica

本草

These detailed monographs are specific to the identification, harvest, preparation, and applications of the herbs we

most frequently find useful in the care of animals. Please keep in mind that this is not an exhaustive list of the herb

resources that are available to you and your pet; it represents only a few that are most familiar to us and other

herbalists who find themselves involved in the care of animals. To list and describe the hundreds of other potentially

useful herbs that exist worldwide would be time and space prohibitive, if not impossible.

这些详细的专着专门针对我们最常发现对动物护理有用的草药的鉴定、收获、制备和应用。请记住，这并

不是您和您的宠物可用的草药资源的详尽列表；它只代表了我们和其他参与动物护理的草药师最熟悉的少

数。列出并描述全世界存在的数百种其他可能有用的草药，即使不是不可能，也是在时间和空间上令人望

而却步。

Despite all measures of scientific study or clinical success that may be in place to validate and substantiate the

efficacy and safety of an herb (or for that matter any medicine), it is important to remember that a golden rule must

never be forgotten: There are no absolutes in nature. Each individual animal is unique so no single herb can be relied

upon to work at the same level of effectiveness in each and every animal.

尽管可以采取所有科学研究或临床成功措施来验证和证实草药（或就此而言任何药物）的功效和安全

性，但重要的是要记住一条黄金法则永远不能忘记：本质上没有绝对。每只动物都是独一无二的，因此没

有一种草药可以对每只动物产生相同的功效。

With this rule in mind, we have also included a supplemental herb list at the end of this chapter where you will

=== PAGE 75 ===
find general information about several other herbs you may find useful in the care of your companion. The herbs in

this list should not be overlooked as lesser or secondary options but as resources worthy of further investigation.

Following is an explanation of the subheads:

考虑到这一规则，我们还在本章末尾提供了补充草药清单，您可以在其中找到有关其他几种草药的一般

信息，这些草药可能对您的伴侣的护理有用。此列表中的草药不应被视为次要或次要选择而被忽视，而应

作为值得进一步研究的资源。以下是对小标题的解释：

Appearance: Under this subheading is a brief physical description of the subject plant. Please keep in mind that the

plant descriptions we provide here are intended only to give you a general idea of what a specific plant looks like.

This book is not intended to serve as a definitive means of plant identification. The process of accurately identifying

a plant involves the use of a highly scientific botanical plant key that enables the user to systematically recognize or

rule out characteristics that are unique to a species. To obtain a botanical key that is specific to plants in your area,

visit your local library or obtain one from a bookstore. To learn how to use a botanical key, consider taking an

introductory botany class at your local college.

外观：该小标题下是主题植物的简要物理描述。请记住，我们在此提供的植物描述仅旨在让您大致了解特

钥，使用户能够系统地识别或排除物种独有的特征。要获取您所在地区植物特有的植物学密钥，请访问当

地的图书馆或从书店获取。要了解如何使用植物学钥匙，请考虑在当地大学参加植物学入门课程。

Habitat and Range: Under this subheading we tell you where you can expect to find the subject plant growing in

the wild. We may also mention which climatic regions are best suited to the cultivation of the plant.

栖息地和范围：在这个小标题下，我们告诉您可以在哪里找到野生生长的主题植物。我们还可以提到哪些

气候地区最适合种植该植物。

Cycle and Bloom Season: Here we inform you of the reproductive characteristics of the plant.

周期和开花季节：在这里我们向您介绍植物的繁殖特征。

Parts Used: Under this subheading we have listed the plant parts (leaves, root, etc.) that are most commonly used

by herbalists.

使用的部分：在此小标题下，我们列出了草药师最常用的植物部分（叶、根等）。

Primary Medicinal Activities: This is not an exhaustive list—most herbs offer dozens of medicinal activities,

many of which may be too weak to be of therapeutic value. Here we have listed the strongest and most predictable

effects the herb is likely to produce when used in a healing context with most animals.

主要药用活性：这并不是一个详尽的列表——大多数草药都提供数十种药用活性，其中许多可能太弱而没

有治疗价值。在这里，我们列出了该草药在对大多数动物进行治疗时可能产生的最强和最可预测的效果。

Strongest Affinities: Under this subheading we have listed the body structures or systems that are likely to benefit

the most from the medicinal activities of the herb.

最强的亲和力：在这个小标题下，我们列出了可能从草药的药用活性中受益最多的身体结构或系统。

Preparation: Here we have listed which types of medicinal preparation (infusion, alcohol tincture, glycerin tincture,

decoction, etc.) are best suited to the use of the herb.

制剂：这里我们列出了最适合使用该草药的药物制剂类型（输液、酒精酊剂、甘油酊剂、汤剂等）。

=== PAGE 76 ===
Common Uses: Under this subheading you will find the “meat” of the monograph. Here we identify and explain

what we feel are the best applications for the herb. This information is a mix of personal opinion, hands-on

experience, clinical observations, and scientific and anecdotal evidence.

常见用途：在此小标题下，您将找到专着的“核心内容”。在这里，我们确定并解释了我们认为该草药的最

佳应用。这些信息综合了个人观点、实践经验、临床观察以及科学和轶事证据。

We’ve included information about scientific studies that we feel are especially relevant to the use of herbs in

animals. We vehemently oppose any form of experimentation that imposes discomfort, disease, or a reduced quality

of life upon an animal. Such experimentation violates the foundations of holistic healing—wellness cannot be

sustained from induced suffering. However, we also feel responsible to the animals who have already suffered or

died at the hands of human science. We must do our best to assure that the knowledge we have gained from their

past suffering is not wasted, and that every shred of useful knowledge that humanity has gained through their

sacrifices is used for other animals in the form of better care and better understanding. In the realm of holistic

healing, there is no need or justification for future animal experimentation—but there is also no point in denying

ourselves or our pets the understanding we have already attained, even if by dark, arrogant means.

我们提供了有关科学研究的信息，我们认为这些信息与在动物身上使用草药特别相关。我们强烈反对任

何会给动物带来不适、疾病或生活质量下降的实验。这种实验违反了整体治疗的基础——健康无法从诱发

的痛苦中维持。然而，我们也对那些已经因人类科学而遭受痛苦或死亡的动物负有责任。我们必须尽最大

努力确保我们从动物过去的痛苦中获得的知识不会被浪费，并且人类通过他们的牺牲获得的每一丝有用的

知识都会以更好的照顾和更好的理解的形式用于其他动物。在整体治疗领域，未来的动物实验没有必要或

合理，但否认我们自己或我们的宠物已经获得的理解也是没有意义的，即使是通过黑暗、傲慢的手段。

Availability: Here you will find information specific to where you can access the herb.

可用性：在这里您可以找到有关在哪里可以获取该药草的具体信息。

Propagation and Harvest: Under this subheading is information about how to grow your own plants or how to

harvest and handle the herb in the wild. If harvesting wild plants interests you, please keep these three important

rules in mind before embarking on any wildcrafting ventures: 1) Do not pick any plants that are endangered or

scarce. 2) Beware of pesticides. Never gather plants from roadsides, cultivated fields, irrigation ditches, or other

areas where weed control efforts may have taken place. 3) You must be 100 percent certain of the identity of the

plant you are picking—before you pick it!

繁殖和收获：此小标题下提供有关如何种植自己的植物或如何在野外收获和处理药草的信息。如果您对收

获野生植物感兴趣，请在开始任何野生植物冒险之前牢记以下三个重要规则：1）不要采摘任何濒临灭绝或

稀有的植物。 2）谨防农药。切勿从路边、耕地、灌溉沟渠或其他可能进行过杂草控制的区域采集植物。

3) 在采摘之前，您必须百分百确定您正在采摘的植物的身份！

Alternatives and Adjuncts: Under this subheading we list and categorize herbs that serve especially well as

alternatives or as complementary additions to the herb we have been discussing throughout the monograph.

替代品和辅助品：在这个小标题下，我们列出并分类了特别适合作为我们在专着中讨论的草药的替代品或

补充品的草药。

Cautions and Comments: Here you will find any contraindications or side effects that we are aware of. You will

also find our comments and opinions relative to the overall safety or potential misuses of the herb.

注意事项和评论：在这里您可以找到我们所知的任何禁忌症或副作用。您还可以找到我们关于该草药的整

参考资料： 用于研究每本专着的大多数科学研究都可以通过互联网在 Medline 网站上获取：

www.medline.gov。

ALEALEA

爱丽雅

Medicago sativa

苜蓿

Pea Family

豌豆家族

Appearance: Alfalfa is a sprawling member of the pea family (Leguminosae) with small, tightly arranged blue or

sometimes pink or white flowers; small, prickly, seed-bearing pods; and cloverlike leaves.

外观：紫花苜蓿是豌豆科（豆科）的一个庞大成员，开着小而紧密排列的蓝色花朵，有时是粉红色或白色

的花朵；小的、多刺的、结有种子的豆荚；和三叶草般的叶子。

Habitat and Range: Widely cultivated throughout the world

栖息地及分布范围：世界各地广泛栽培

Cycle and Bloom Season: A perennial that first blooms in early summer, alfalfa continues to bloom after

successive harvests throughout the growing season as long as the climate permits vigorous regrowth.

周期和开花季节：苜蓿是一种在初夏首次开花的多年生植物，只要气候允许旺盛的再生能力，在整个生长

季节连续收获后就会继续开花。

Parts Used: Dried leaves, stems, unopened flowers

使用部分：干叶、茎、未开的花

Primary Medicinal Activities: Nutritive, anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, stimulates urination (diuretic)

主要药用活性：营养、抗炎、抗氧化、刺激排尿（利尿）

Strongest Affinities: Musculoskeletal system, digestive tract, liver

最强的亲和力：肌肉骨骼系统、消化道、肝脏

Preparation: Capsules, infusion, liquid extract, or dried bulk herb sprinkled onto food

制备方法：胶囊、输液、液体提取物或干散装药草撒在食物上

Common Uses: Alfalfa contains a broad spectrum of nutrients, including considerable quantities of protein (up to

50 percent by weight), trace minerals, dietary fiber, and vitamins A, B1, B12, C, D, E, and K. It is also high in

chlorophyll, which serves as an antioxidant in the bloodstream. All of this makes alfalfa particularly attractive as a

livestock feed. In addition to being highly nutritive, alfalfa is traditionally known as one of the best herbal

treatments for arthritis, rheumatism, and gout. Clinical research of the use of alfalfa in treating these diseases has

shown that at least 10 to 20 percent of human subjects experience dramatic reduction of painful symptoms.

Traditional uses in animals have commonly led to similar results. For arthritis and other inflammatory diseases of

=== PAGE 79 ===
the joints, alfalfa can bring long-term relief to dogs, cats, rodents, and horses and various other herbivores who

receive it as a daily food supplement. By now you probably see the value of this herb in the care of older animals.

For use in therapeutic doses, it works well when combined with dandelion, yucca, and licorice.

常见用途：苜蓿含有广泛的营养成分，包括大量蛋白质（按重量计高达 50%）、微量矿物质、膳食纤维和

维生素 A、B 1 、B 12

Medicago sativa

苜蓿

Alfalfa possesses cancer-preventive qualities as well. It is believed that alfalfa induces complex cellular activities

that serve to inactivate chemical carcinogens in the liver and small intestine before they can cause damage, thus

helping to reduce the risk of cancerous growths.

苜蓿还具有预防癌症的功效。据信，苜蓿能诱导复杂的细胞活动，从而在肝脏和小肠中的化学致癌物造

成损害之前将其灭活，从而有助于降低癌生长的风险。

Alfalfa’s considerable vitamin K content has been shown to be beneficial in remedying bleeding disorders that

may result from long-term use of antibiotics, anticoagulants, aspirin, and anticonvulsant drugs. The coumarin

constituent of alfalfa is also well known for its anticoagulant qualities, and in fact many anticlotting drugs were

derived from this compound. Excessive doses of fresh alfalfa or concentrated extracts may be contraindicated in

animals with anemia, but moderate dietary supplementation may be useful in some types of this disease.

苜蓿中大量的维生素 K 含量已被证明有助于治疗因长期使用抗生素、抗凝剂、阿司匹林和抗惊厥药物可

能导致的出血性疾病。苜蓿的香豆素成分也以其抗凝血特性而闻名，事实上许多抗凝血药物都是从这种化

合物中提取的。对于患有贫血的动物，过量服用新鲜苜蓿或浓缩提取物可能是禁忌，但适度的膳食补充剂

可能对某些类型的这种疾病有用。

The various saponin constituents of alfalfa are known to help with the absorption of fat-soluble nutrients in the

small intestine and may act to stimulate the body’s natural production of growth hormones—yet another reason for

=== PAGE 80 ===
its popularity as a livestock feed. In this capacity, alfalfa works by mechanisms very similar to those of yucca, but it

is much less irritating to the stomach and intestines than yucca and therefore can be used over longer periods without

adverse side effects. It may be especially useful in animals with debilitating diseases who need to gain weight but

cannot afford added stress upon compromised body systems.

众所周知，苜蓿的各种皂苷成分有助于小肠中脂溶性营养物质的吸收，并可能刺激人体自然产生生长激

素——这也是其作为牲畜饲料受欢迎的另一个原因。在这种能力上，苜蓿的作用机制与丝兰非常相似，但

它对胃和肠道的刺激比丝兰小得多，因此可以长期使用而不会产生不良副作用。对于患有使人衰弱的疾病

的动物来说，它可能特别有用，这些动物需要增加体重，但无法承受受损身体系统的额外压力。

In the urinary tract, alfalfa has an alkalinizing effect, making it useful in treating ailments that involve overly

acidic urine, especially where there is bladder irritation and crystal formation. This nutritional plant also helps an

animal adjust to a new diet.

在泌尿道中，苜蓿具有碱化作用，可用于治疗涉及尿液过酸的疾病，尤其是膀胱刺激和晶体形成的疾

病。这种营养植物还可以帮助动物适应新的饮食。

For the brain, alfalfa is said to help improve mental vigor. This is likely due to alfalfa’s broad spectrum of

nutrients, many of which are critical to proper nerve and brain functions.

对于大脑来说，苜蓿据说有助于提高精神活力。这可能是由于苜蓿含有广泛的营养物质，其中许多对神

经和大脑的正常功能至关重要。

Availability: Health food stores; can be propagated in a home garden

购买地点：保健食品店；可以在家庭花园中繁殖

Propagation and Harvest: Alfalfa is extremely easy to grow just about anywhere. In fact, if allowed to spread, it

quickly becomes competitive with everything else in the garden. Being a legume, alfalfa changes nitrogen into a

usable form within its extensive root system, making it a valuable soil-building ingredient when the plants are tilled

in. Unfortunately, the weedlike character of this plant overshadows its value as a soil builder. Digging the roots is

like pulling crabgrass, and tilling often results in even greater proliferation from the subsequent root cuttings. In

other words, buy certified organic alfalfa at an herb store, unless you wish to delegate a portion (or perhaps all) of

your garden to it. (A word of caution to the insistent gardener: If you plant alfalfa and then have second thoughts

about keeping it, remove it before it goes to seed. Once it does, it’s yours for life!)

繁殖和收获：苜蓿在任何地方都非常容易种植。事实上，如果让它蔓延，它很快就会与花园里的其他植物

竞争。作为一种豆科植物，苜蓿在其广泛的根系中将氮转化为可用的形式，使其成为植物翻耕时有价值的

土壤建设成分。不幸的是，这种植物的杂草特性掩盖了其作为土壤建设者的价值。挖根就像拔马唐一样，

耕耘通常会导致随后的根插条更加增殖。换句话说，请在药草店购买经过认证的有机苜蓿，除非您希望将

花园的一部分（或可能全部）委托给它。 （对坚持不懈的园丁的忠告：如果您种植了苜蓿，然后又考虑保

留它，请在它结籽之前将其除去。一旦结籽，它就属于您一生！）

Gather alfalfa before it comes into bloom. Cut (or mow) the plants during dry weather, cutting the stems at about

1 inch above ground level. Allow the herb to dry in an airy, moisture-free place that is away from direct sunlight

until it is completely dry, or make a tincture from the freshly cut greens.

在苜蓿开花之前收集它。在干燥的天气里切割（或割草）植物，在距地面约 1 英寸的地方切割茎。将药

草放在通风、干燥、避免阳光直射的地方干燥，直至完全干燥，或者用刚切下的绿色蔬菜制成酊剂。

Alternatives and Adjuncts: Dandelion, garlic, licorice, red clover, and yucca

替代品和辅助品：蒲公英、大蒜、甘草、红三叶草和丝兰

Cautions and Comments: Alfalfa is regarded as safe by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA). Although

adverse side effects are rare, many horse owners testify that consumption of too much fresh alfalfa may lead to colic,

a condition that can be serious in animals. This is due in large part to alfalfa’s saponin constituents. Although these

=== PAGE 81 ===
soaplike compounds are medicinally valuable, used in excess they may irritate the stomach lining and intestinal

mucosa, resulting in nausea and gastritis. Horses and rabbits cannot vomit, which greatly compounds the seriousness

of this side effect. The risk of colic occurring is greatly reduced by feeding only dried greens.

注意事项和评论：美国食品和药物管理局 (FDA) 认为苜蓿是安全的。尽管不良副作用很少见，但许多马主

证明，食用过多的新鲜苜蓿可能会导致绞痛，这种情况对动物来说可能很严重。这在很大程度上是由于苜

蓿的皂苷成分。尽管这些肥皂状化合物具有药用价值，但过量使用可能会刺激胃壁和肠粘膜，导致恶心和

胃炎。马和兔子不能呕吐，这极大地加剧了这种副作用的严重性。只喂干蔬菜可以大大降低发生绞痛的风

险。

The seeds of alfalfa have been found to contain a toxic amino acid, l-canavanine, which has caused blood

disorders in humans and in animals. Use alfalfa only during its prebloom stages of growth. Alfalfa can trigger

allergic responses in animals who are especially sensitive to pollens.

人们发现苜蓿种子含有一种有毒氨基酸，即左旋刀豆氨酸，它会导致人类和动物的血液疾病。仅在开花

前的生长阶段使用苜蓿。苜蓿可以引发对花粉特别敏感的动物的过敏反应。

=== PAGE 82 ===
ALOE

芦荟

Aloe spp.

芦荟属

Lily Family

百合家族

Appearance: Aloes are cactuslike members of the lily family (Liliaceae), having narrow, tapering, proportionately

thick, succulent leaves with spiny margins. There are perhaps five hundred species of aloe, but the most common

aloe of commerce is Aloe barbadensis, which we commonly know as aloe vera. This species produces its leaves

directly from a stout central stalk, in a rosette fashion, while several other varieties of aloe are branched, almost

bushlike. Aside from these variations, all aloes share a similar appearance and can grow very large. In some areas of

southwestern Africa, aloes are seen in excess of 25 feet tall with stems more than 10 feet in circumference. Flowers

are small, tubular, characteristically lilylike in appearance, and are produced in leafless, terminal spikes.

外观：芦荟是百合科（百合科）的仙人掌成员，具有狭窄、逐渐变细、厚度适当、多汁的叶子，边缘有

刺。芦荟大约有五百种，但最常见的商业芦荟是库拉索芦荟，我们通常称为芦荟。该物种的叶子直接从粗

壮的中央茎上长出，呈莲座状，而其他几种芦荟品种是分枝的，几乎像灌木丛。除了这些差异之外，所有

芦荟都有相似的外观并且可以长得很大。在非洲西南部的一些地区，芦荟高度超过 25 英尺，茎周长超过 10

英尺。花小，管状，外观典型地像百合，形成无叶、顶生穗状花序。

Habitat and Range: Aloes are indigenous to southern and eastern Africa and have been introduced to the West

Indies, where a great deal of commercial cultivation takes place. In areas of North America and Europe with

Mediterranean climates, aloes are used as landscape and garden plants. They are popular indoor plants throughout

much of the world.

栖息地和分布范围：芦荟原产于非洲南部和东部，现已被引入西印度群岛，那里有大量的商业种植。在北

美和欧洲的地中海气候地区，芦荟被用作景观和园林植物。它们是世界各地流行的室内植物。

Cycle and Bloom Season: Aloes are perennials that bloom opportunistically when mature. In other words, if they

receive all of the elements they require to thrive, they will likely remain in bloom throughout each year of their lives.

周期和开花季节：芦荟是多年生植物，成熟时会机会性地开花。换句话说，如果它们获得了茁壮成长所需

的所有元素，它们很可能会在生命中的每一年都保持盛开。

Parts Used: Primarily the gel-like juice of the inner leaf or the yellowish latex contained immediately beneath the

skin of the leaves

使用部分：主要是内叶的凝胶状汁液或叶皮下紧邻的黄色乳胶

Primary Medicinal Activities: Wound healing (vulnerary), soothes skin (emollient), anti-bacterial, antioxidant,

stimulates the immune system (immunostimulant), anticancer, antitumor, cooling to the skin.

主要药用活性：伤口愈合（创伤）、舒缓皮肤（润肤）、抗菌、抗氧化、刺激免疫系统（免疫刺激）、抗

癌、抗肿瘤、给皮肤降温。

=== PAGE 83 ===
Strongest Affinities: Skin, digestive system, lymph system

最强亲和力：皮肤、消化系统、淋巴系统

Preparation: Freshly pressed juice or stabilized (commercial) aloe gel preparations are the most commonly used

forms of aloe. Using this plant at home is as easy as cutting a mature leaf from the lower part of the plant and

squeezing out the juice. Intravenous formulations of aloe ingredients have been FDA-approved and are available for

use by veterinarians. Acemannan, a chemical compound found in aloe vera juice, is a powerful immunostimulant.

制备：鲜榨果汁或稳定（商业）芦荟凝胶制剂是最常用的芦荟形式。在家里使用这种植物就像从植物下部

切下一片成熟的叶子并挤出汁液一样简单。芦荟成分的静脉制剂已获得 FDA 批准，可供兽医使用。

Acemannan 是芦荟汁中发现的一种化合物，是一种强大的免疫刺激剂。

Common Uses: Aloe’s great claim to fame is from its use as a topical skin dressing. Fresh aloe juice or

commercially prepared gel contains dozens of minerals, proteins, enzymes, polysaccharides, and other elements that

help soften and soothe the skin and promote the rapid healing of minor burns and wounds. Topical application of

aloe gel will likely bring immediate, cooling relief to fleabites, poison ivy, and sunburns. It is also excellent for

reducing the itch and tightening of postsurgical incisions. Applied after sutures are removed, the gel reduces much

of the irritation that so often leads to persistent chewing or scratching and may result in inflammation and infection.

In any external application, apply enough juice to lightly cover the affected area and allow it to dry. If possible, keep

the animal from licking it off—the idea is to leave the juice on as long as possible. Unless your animal has an

adverse reaction to the juice (such as reddening or an allergy rash), aloe can be applied liberally once or twice per

day until the healing process is progressing well.

常见用途：芦荟因其用作局部皮肤敷料而闻名。新鲜的芦荟汁或商业制备的凝胶含有数十种矿物质、蛋白

质、酶、多糖和其他元素，有助于软化和舒缓皮肤，促进轻微烧伤和伤口的快速愈合。局部使用芦荟凝胶

可能会立即缓解跳蚤、毒藤和晒伤的症状。它对于减少瘙痒和收紧术后切口也非常有效。拆线后使用凝

胶，可以减少很多刺激，而刺激通常会导致持续咀嚼或抓伤，并可能导致炎症和感染。在任何外部应用

中，应用足够的汁液轻轻覆盖受影响的区域并使其干燥。如果可能的话，不要让动物舔掉它——我们的想

法是尽可能长时间地保留汁液。除非您的动物对果汁有不良反应（例如变红或过敏皮疹），否则可以每天

大量使用芦荟一次或两次，直到愈合过程进展顺利。

Internally, a small dose of aloe juice may be useful for healing minor injuries and irritations of the digestive tract,

such as those that may occur when Bowser swallows a jagged bone.

在内部，小剂量的芦荟汁可能有助于治愈消化道的轻微损伤和刺激，例如鲍泽吞下锯齿状骨头时可能发

生的情况。

Scientists have recently found that acemannan acts as a strong immunostimulant in animals, particularly in cats. It

has been found to be especially effective in the treatment of fibrosarcoma and feline leukemia virus (FeLV). It is

theorized that acemannan triggers an increase in the autoimmune attack upon the viruses believed to cause these

usually fatal diseases. Typically, over 70 percent of cats who become ill with FeLV die within ten weeks of the

onset of disease. But in a recent study, forty-four cats with confirmed FeLV were injected with 2 milligrams per

kilogram of acemannan weekly for six weeks and reexamined six weeks after the treatment ended. At the end of the

twelve-week study, 71 percent of the cats were alive and in good health. Acemannan has also been shown to be

effective against cancerous tumors in rodents and dogs. It has been FDA approved for veterinary use and will

undoubtedly be tested in humans.

科学家最近发现乙酰甘露聚糖对动物（尤其是猫）具有很强的免疫刺激剂作用。人们发现它对于治疗纤

维肉瘤和猫白血病病毒（FeLV）特别有效。据推测，乙酰甘露聚糖会引发对病毒的自身免疫攻击的增加，

这些病毒被认为会导致这些通常致命的疾病。通常，超过 70% 感染 FeLV 的猫会在发病后十周内死亡。但

在最近的一项研究中，44 只确诊为 FeLV 的猫每周注射 2 毫克/公斤的乙酰甘露聚糖，持续六周，并在治疗

结束后六周进行重新检查。在为期 12 周的研究结束时，71% 的猫还活着并且健康状况良好。乙酰甘露聚糖

还被证明可以有效对抗啮齿动物和狗的癌性肿瘤。它已获得 FDA 批准用于兽医用途，并且无疑将在人体中

进行测试。

=== PAGE 84 ===
Aloe barbadensis

库拉索芦荟

Other chemical compounds found in aloe juice have been shown to have antioxidant actions in the body.

芦荟汁中发现的其他化合物已被证明在体内具有抗氧化作用。

Availability: Aloe gel or juice (the difference being consistency) is available at health food stores. Any good

nursery has the plants.

可用性：芦荟凝胶或果汁（区别在于稠度）可在保健食品商店购买。任何好的苗圃都有植物。

Propagation and Harvest: Aloe is easy to grow as a houseplant. It requires well-drained, sandy soil and should be

watered only once or twice a month. Avoid using potting soil—it retains too much moisture and may cause rot

problems. Ordinary garden soil will do fine. A happy aloe that receives plenty of sunlight will bloom continuously

and reproduce aggressively from side-shoots. These shoots are easily transplanted into separate pots. If you live in

an area where frost is rare, aloe can be planted in a garden. Again, just give it plenty of sun, don’t overwater it, and it

will be yours forever.

繁殖和收获：芦荟很容易作为室内植物种植。它需要排水良好的沙质土壤，每月只需浇水一到两次。避免

使用盆栽土——它会保留过多的水分，并可能导致腐烂问题。普通的花园土壤就可以了。接受充足阳光的

幸福芦荟会持续开花，并从侧枝积极繁殖。这些芽很容易移植到单独的盆中。如果你住在很少霜冻的地

区，可以在花园里种植芦荟。再说一遍，只要给它充足的阳光，不要浇水过多，它就会永远属于你。

Alternatives and Adjuncts: Nothing really compares with aloe, but if you don’t have it around, look toward

chickweed, plantain, self-heal, and comfrey as topical alternatives. Internally, ginger, cayenne, red clover, cleavers,

dandelion, yarrow, garlic, and burdock are worth considering to complement the activity of aloe.

=== PAGE 85 ===
替代品和辅助品：没有什么能真正与芦荟相比，但如果你手边没有芦荟，可以考虑使用繁缕、车前草、自

愈剂和紫草作为外用替代品。在内部，生姜、辣椒、红三叶草、菜刀、蒲公英、西洋蓍草、大蒜和牛蒡值

得考虑来补充芦荟的活性。

Cautions and Comments: Aloe juice, although bitter, is generally safe for internal or external uses in dogs, cats and

most other animal types. However, be cautious of any products containing “Aloes.” Aloes consists of a sticky latex

that is extracted from the inner skin of aloe leaves. This latex possesses strong purgative qualities that may result in

digestive distress and severe diarrhea. Although several commercial laxative preparations use aloe latex in their

formulas, we strongly discourage their use in animals. It is believed that aloe components may be passed in mother’s

milk to nursing infants, so it should not be used in such circumstances.

注意事项和评论：芦荟汁虽然苦，但对于狗、猫和大多数其他动物类型的内服或外用通常是安全的。但

是，请谨慎对待任何含有“芦荟”的产品。芦荟由从芦荟叶内皮中提取的粘性乳胶组成。这种乳胶具有很强

的泻药特性，可能会导致消化不良和严重腹泻。尽管一些商业泻药制剂在其配方中使用芦荟乳胶，但我们

强烈反对将其用于动物。据认为，芦荟成分可能会通过母乳传递给哺乳婴儿，因此在这种情况下不应该使

用。

=== PAGE 86 ===
ARNICA

山金车

Arnica spp.

山金车属

Sunflower Family

向日葵家族

Appearance: Arnica is a classic sunflower with bright yellow daisylike flowers. Leaves oppose one another on the

stem and range from narrowly lance shaped to broadly heart shaped (depending on species). The leaves and stems of

most species are at least partially covered with fine hairs. Most arnicas are aromatic, particularly when the leaves are

bruised, with a distinctive pinelike odor. Arnicas are small plants, seldom exceeding 12 inches in height.

外观：山金车是一种经典的向日葵，花朵呈亮黄色雏菊状。叶子在茎上彼此相对，形状从狭长的矛状到宽

大的心形（取决于物种）。大多数物种的叶子和茎至少部分覆盖有细毛。大多数山金车都是芳香的，特别

是当叶子被碰伤时，具有独特的松树气味。山金车是小型植物，高度很少超过 12 英寸。

Habitat and Range: Arnica is a mountain plant that occurs in coniferous subalpine and alpine regions of western

North America from Alaska to the mountains of southern California, where it grows only above 9,000 feet in

elevation.

栖息地和分布范围：山金车是一种山地植物，生长于北美西部从阿拉斯加到南加州山区的针叶亚高山和高

山地区，仅生长在海拔 9,000 英尺以上。

Cycle and Bloom Season: Arnica is a perennial that blooms during its second year of growth and every year

thereafter. It is among the first flowers to bloom in early spring and is often one of the first to die back in early

summer. During dry years, arnica may not bloom at all.

周期和开花季节：山金车是一种多年生植物，在生长的第二年和此后每年都会开花。它是早春最早绽放的

Common Uses: Arnica is used for closed-tissue injuries, including fractures, sprains, and contusions. It is perhaps

the best-known herbal sports medicine. Used topically, preparations of arnica act to open up peripheral capillaries

and lymph ducts and increase circulation in tissues that are engorged with fluids as a result of injury. When used

immediately after an injury occurs, results can be dramatic. In essence, arnica helps to speed the healing process by

moving wastebound fluids out and moving cleansing fluids and platelets into the affected area. Arnica is especially

valuable for treatment of horses and other large animals who are subjected to rigorous exercise and an occasional

twist or strain of the leg or hip joints. Arnica can be used on dogs as well, but special measures must be taken to

prohibit the animal from licking it off because arnica can be toxic if taken internally in improper dosages. Cats are

not excluded from the use of arnica, but they are more sensitive to arnica’s volatile oils and are more prone to

allergic reactions with this herb as they are with so many other substances. Test a small portion of your cat’s skin

before using arnica for an injury. Look for development of redness or other signs of irritation.

常见用途：山金车用于治疗闭合组织损伤，包括骨折、扭伤和挫伤。它可能是最著名的草药运动药物。局

部使用时，山金车制剂可以打开外周毛细血管和淋巴管，并增加因受伤而充满液体的组织的循环。如果受

伤后立即使用，效果可能会很显着。从本质上讲，山金车通过将废物结合的液体排出并将清洁液和血小板

移入受影响的区域来帮助加速愈合过程。山金车对于治疗马和其他大型动物特别有价值，这些动物需要进

行剧烈运动，并且腿部或髋关节偶尔会扭曲或拉伤。山金车也可以用于狗，但必须采取特殊措施禁止动物

舔掉它，因为如果内服剂量不当，山金车可能有毒。猫并不排除使用山金车，但它们对山金车的挥发油更

敏感，并且更容易对这种草药产生过敏反应，就像它们对许多其他物质一样。在使用山金车治疗伤口之

前，先测试猫的一小部分皮肤。观察是否出现发红或其他刺激迹象。

To use arnica on a dog or cat, apply enough of the infusion or gel to wet the skin of the animal (not just the fur),

then wrap the area with gauze or a piece of cloth and secure it so the animal cannot easily remove it. The idea is to

keep the preparation on the animal as long as possible. Arnica can be applied this way twice daily for up to three

days. Long-term applications should not be necessary and are not recommended because a rash is likely to develop

from overuse.

要在狗或猫身上使用山金车，请涂抹足够的输液或凝胶以润湿动物的皮肤（不仅仅是毛皮），然后用纱

布或一块布包裹该区域并固定，以免动物轻易去除它。我们的想法是尽可能长时间地在动物身上进行准

备。山金车可以这样使用，每天两次，最多三天。不需要也不建议长期使用，因为过度使用可能会出现皮

疹。

When used internally in carefully measured doses, arnica is said to act as a neurological device in cases of chronic

urinary incontinence that cannot be attributed to physiological pathologies. While use of arnica in this capacity holds

a great deal of promise for many animals suffering from urinary incontinence, the toxicity of this plant limits such

use to the advanced professional. Talk with a holistic veterinarian if you are interested in this use.

当以仔细测量的剂量内部使用时，山金车据说可以在不能归因于生理病理的慢性尿失禁的情况下充当神

级专业人员的这种用途。如果您对此用途感兴趣，请咨询整体兽医。

Although this book focuses on herbal remedies, the value of arnica in homeopathic preparations should not be

Propagation and Harvest: Arnica requires soil with plenty of organic matter and does best when its root system

can crawl around under a blanket of pine needles. Given that it is seldom found at altitudes under 3,000 feet except

in Canada, it likely has some specialized light- or air-quality requirements that prohibit it from flourishing in urban

areas. If you live in the mountains, arnica can be grown from seeds or root cuttings. But beware—the roots will

繁殖和收获：山金车需要含有大量有机质的土壤，当其根系可以在松针覆盖下爬行时效果最佳。鉴于除加

吞噬你的花园。

To harvest arnica from the wild, grasp the stem of the flowering herb just above ground level, then snap it off,

taking only what you need. Take care not to damage the roots by pulling on the plant or stepping into a patch of

plants—the roots crawl horizontally, and the pressure of a human foot can injure them.

要从野外收获山金车，请抓住开花草本植物高于地面的茎，然后将其折断，只取所需的部分。小心不要

place. Fresh plants yield a more potent infusion but spoil quickly in the refrigerator because of their water content.

Regardless, we opt for the use of fresh arnica. To learn how to make an oil infusion, refer to chapter 1.

Another option for the use of arnica in emergency situations is to make a simple poultice by mashing a flowering

ASTRAGALUS

黄芪

Astragalus membranaceous

膜质黄芪

Pea Family

豌豆家族

Appearance: A typical member of the pea family, astragalus has finely divided leaves, small pealike flowers and

seed pods, and a sprawling, vinelike stature that brings to mind any of the hundreds of wild vetches that inhabit

much of the globe. Astragalus membranaceous, the species of commerce, may grow as tall as 6 feet, which gives it

an appearance that is similar to licorice (Glycyrrhiza spp.), yet another member of the pea family. There is a growing

belief among herbalists, botanists, and medical researchers that North American milk vetch (A. americana), a

common weed, may have similar medicinal attributes and may even be the same plant as A. membranaceous, the

medicinal astragalus of commerce. The Astragalus genus is large, consisting of hundreds of species, which in many

cases are difficult to differentiate even by trained botanists. Some varieties of Astragalus are toxic, and to compound

this mystery even more, these plants often cross-pollinate and hybridize. For now, no one knows whether or not we

have a wild, medicinal Astragalus in North America.

外观：黄芪是豌豆科的典型成员，具有细碎的叶子、豌豆般的小花和种子荚，以及蔓生的藤蔓状身材，让

人想起栖息在地球大部分地区的数百种野生野豌豆。黄芪是一种商业物种，可长到 6 英尺高，这使其外观

类似于豌豆科的另一种成员甘草 (Glycyrrhiza spp.)。草药学家、植物学家和医学研究人员越来越相信，北美

紫云英（A. americana）这种常见杂草可能具有相似的药用特性，甚至可能与商业药用黄芪为同一种植物。

。黄芪属很大，由数百个物种组成，在许多情况下，即使是训练有素的植物学家也很难区分。黄芪的某些

品种是有毒的，为了使这个谜团更加复杂，这些植物经常异花授粉和杂交。目前，没有人知道北美是否有

一种野生的药用黄芪。

Habitat and Range: An import from China, Astragalus has been cultivated throughout much of the world as an

important herb of commerce.

栖息地和分布范围：黄芪是从中国进口的，作为一种重要的商业药草在世界大部分地区都有种植。

Cycle and Bloom Season: A perennial that blooms from spring to early summer

周期和开花季节：从春季到初夏开花的多年生植物

Common Uses: One of the best known and widely used herbs in Chinese medicine (where the herb is known as

huang qi), astragalus has found its way into Western herbalism by virtue of its widely versatile immune-

strengthening qualities. In Chinese medicine, astragalus root is considered sweet and mildly warm, tonifying the qi

(pronounced “chee”) and hoisting the yang. (Sweet and warm are terms used in Chinese medicine to describe an

herb’s relation to the body’s energy flows and do not relate to flavor.) Astragalus root is commonly used for spleen

and lung qi deficiency, including symptoms of emaciation, weariness, shortness of breath, loss of appetite, diarrhea,

and prolapse of the uterus or anus.

常见用途：黄芪是中药中最著名和广泛使用的草药之一（该草药被称为黄芪），凭借其广泛的多功能免疫

增强特性而进入西方草药学。中医认为，黄芪味甘、微温，具有补气升阳的作用。 （甘、温是中医术语，

描述一种草药与人体能量流动的关系，与味道无关。）黄芪常用于治疗脾肺气虚，包括消瘦、疲倦、气短

的症状、食欲不振、腹泻、子宫或肛门脱垂。

Astragalus is especially useful for strengthening the body against viral infections of the respiratory tract and heart

through stimulation of killer-cell activity and interferon production in the body. It imparts direct antibacterial and

anti-inflammatory qualities to this effort as well. Astragalus is a viable option for early treatment of various forms of

respiratory infection, including kennel cough (Bordetella bronchiseptica), a condition that theoretically involves this

bacterium’s opportunistic cooperation with various forms of virus. While astragalus works to stimulate T cell

activity and helps to raise white blood cell counts, it also boosts the body’s defenses through its liver-strengthening

attributes. In a study involving rats, saponin constituents were shown to enhance DNA synthesis in the liver—a

process believed to be a major factor in the strengthening of cell structures against infection or the introduction of

toxins. Other studies suggest that astragalus may be useful for helping the body protect itself and speed recovery

from the damaging effects of long-term steroid therapies. Astragalus is known to strengthen kidney circulation,

making it useful in early stages of kidney infection or renal failure.

黄芪通过刺激体内杀伤细胞活性和干扰素产生，特别有助于增强身体抵抗呼吸道和心脏病毒感染的能

力。它还为这项工作赋予了直接的抗菌和抗炎特性。黄芪是早期治疗各种形式的呼吸道感染的可行选择，

Propagation and Harvest: Astragalus is easy to grow from seed—some rich soil, full sun, and ample watering are

蜂香膏

Monarda spp.

美洲薄荷属

Mint Family

薄荷家族

Appearance: This pungent genus of dry land mints is known by many common names: wild bergamot, purple bee

balm, horsemint, wild oregano, Oswego tea, and sweet leaf. Leaves are lance shaped, oppose one another on the

stem, and have a tendency to curve backward toward the ground. Leaf margins are sometimes, but not always,

toothed. Like most members of the mint family, the stems of bee balm are distinctively square (four-sided). Flowers

are presented in clusters at the top of the plant, each containing dozens of tiny, rose- to purple-colored blossoms.

Perhaps the most distinguishing characteristic of this plant is its strong but pleasant odor, which ranges from sweetly

sagelike to that which leads many to believe they have discovered a wild strain of oregano. The plant can grow to 3

feet on its sturdy stems, but most are found in the range of 6 to 18 inches tall.

外观：这种辛辣的旱地薄荷属植物有许多俗名：野生佛手柑、紫蜂香脂、马薄荷、野生牛至、奥斯威戈茶

和甜叶。叶子呈矛状，在茎上彼此相对，并且有向后弯曲到地面的倾向。叶缘有时但并非总是有齿。与薄

荷家族的大多数成员一样，蜂香膏的茎呈独特的方形（四边形）。花朵成簇出现在植物的顶部，每朵都含

有数十朵微小的玫瑰色到紫色的花朵。也许这种植物最显着的特征是其强烈而令人愉悦的气味，从甜美的

鼠尾草气味到让许多人相信他们发现了野生牛至品种的气味。这种植物在其坚固的茎上可以长到 3 英尺，

但大多数高度在 6 到 18 英寸之间。

Habitat and Range: Wild bee balm likes meadows and slopes that are predominantly dry and sunny. Unlike most

mints, bee balm is drought tolerant and prefers dry land habitats. Bee balm (M. fistulosa) is generally found at

elevations below 4,000 feet. Other varieties of Monarda, such as M. menthaefolia, grow at higher elevations in

shady, moist soils.

栖息地和范围：野生蜂香膏喜欢干燥和阳光充足的草地和斜坡。与大多数薄荷糖不同，蜂香脂具有耐旱

性，更喜欢干燥的土地栖息地。蜂香膏 (M. fistulosa) 通常出现在海拔 4,000 英尺以下的地方。其他美国薄荷

品种，例如薄荷薄荷，生长在海拔较高、阴凉潮湿的土壤中。

The range of this plant remains largely undefined, but in the U.S. it seems to be spreading westward from the east.

Livestock enjoy grazing on this plant and have undoubtedly served as a vehicle in the expansion of bee balm’s

range.

这种植物的分布范围在很大程度上仍不明确，但在美国，它似乎正在从东部向西蔓延。牲畜喜欢在这种

植物上吃草，这无疑成为了扩大蜂膏范围的工具。

Cycle and Bloom Season: A perennial that blooms by midsummer and often continues to bloom until the first frost

周期和开花季节：一种多年生植物，在仲夏开花，通常持续开花直到第一次霜冻

Parts Used: Leaves plucked from the plant; the entire aerial plant if the stem is taken

使用部分：从植物中摘下的叶子；整个气生植物（如果取茎）

Primary Medicinal Activities: promotes sweating (diaphoretic), expels intestinal gas (carminative), antiseptic,

=== PAGE 95 ===
reduces pain (analgesic), antifungal

主要药用活性：促进出汗（发汗）、排出肠气（驱风）、抗菌、减轻疼痛（镇痛）、抗真菌

Strongest Affinities: Skin, mouth, digestive tract, kidneys, urinary tract

亲和力最强：皮肤、口腔、消化道、肾脏、泌尿道

Monarda fistulosa

福氏美国薄荷

Preparation: Unlike most leafy herbs, which begin to break down and lose their potency after about six months,

bee balm can be dried and stored for up to two years. The fresh or dried leaf, stem, and flower material can be made

into an alcohol or glycerin tincture. The dried plant can be infused for use in skin and eyewashes.

准备工作：与大多数叶草植物不同的是，大多数叶草植物在大约六个月后开始分解并失去效力，而蜂香膏

可以干燥并保存长达两年。新鲜或干燥的叶、茎、花材料可制成酒精或甘油酊剂。干燥的植物可用于皮肤

和洗眼液。

Common Uses: Although this plant is widely available and infinitely useful, it is often overlooked by herbalists, and

it has not received the clinical study that it deserves as a healing ally. Despite an overall lack of scientific validation,

bee balm is a safe herb to use in both animals and humans. Many North American Indian tribes used this plant

extensively for healing and in spiritual ceremonies.

常见用途：虽然这种植物用途广泛且用途无限，但它经常被草药医生所忽视，而且它还没有得到作为治疗

盟友的临床研究。尽管总体上缺乏科学验证，蜂香膏是一种可安全用于动物和人类的草药。许多北美印第

安部落广泛使用这种植物进行治疗和精神仪式。

Like most mints, bee balm has a special affinity toward the digestive tract, where it is useful for relieving gastritis

=== PAGE 96 ===
and spastic colon. However, it does not taste good, and most herbivores abandon it in favor of less pungent forage.

Therefore, for use as a digestive aid in animals, the best form of administering bee balm is gelatin capsules (gel

capsules) or a glycerin extract.

与大多数薄荷糖一样，蜂香膏对消化道有特殊的亲和力，可有效缓解胃炎和痉挛性结肠。然而，它的味

道并不好，大多数食草动物放弃它，转而选择不太刺激的饲料。因此，作为动物消化助剂，蜂香膏的最佳

给药形式是明胶胶囊（凝胶胶囊）或甘油提取物。

Bee balm has excellent antibacterial qualities and is especially useful for mouth and gum infections. Two methods

of application work here: a poultice can be made from the dried or fresh herb and applied directly to the affected

area, or a strong infusion or tincture can be used the same way. The poultice or infusion can also be effective as an

antifungal agent. Dogs, cats, and horses and other large animals with fungal infections of the skin are likely to

benefit from a generous topical application of bee balm poultice or salve or from twice-daily skin rinses with cooled

bee balm tea (also see “Calendula”). To make the tea, cover a generous handful of the herb with hot water and allow

it to steep until the water has thoroughly cooled. Don’t worry about straining the herb—just pour the entire mixture

over the affected areas of the animal. In dry weather, or in cases where the animal chooses to lick the rinse off before

it can be effective, you might consider applying the tea as a fomentation (see chapter 1). Bee balm skin rinses also

can bring soothing relief to itchy skin that has resulted from infected fleabites or spontaneous dermatitis (commonly

caused by poison ivy, nettle stings, or contact allergic reactions) and help to relieve pain while reducing scarring

from minor burns. The rinse also imparts a pleasant odor to your pet.

蜂香膏具有出色的抗菌性能，对口腔和牙龈感染特别有效。这里有两种使用方法：可以用干燥或新鲜的

草药制成膏剂，直接涂抹在患处，或者以同样的方式使用浓汤或酊剂。膏剂或输液也可以有效地作为抗真

菌剂。狗、猫、马和其他患有皮肤真菌感染的大型动物可能会受益于大量局部涂抹蜂胶膏或药膏，或者每

天两次用冷蜂胶茶冲洗皮肤（另见“金盏花”） 。泡茶时，将一大把药草倒入热水中，浸泡直至水完全冷

却。不用担心过滤草药——只需将整个混合物倒在动物受影响的区域即可。在干燥的天气里，或者在动物

选择在冲洗液发挥作用之前将其舔掉的情况下，您可以考虑使用茶作为热敷剂（参见第 1 章）。蜂香膏皮

肤冲洗液还可以舒缓因跳蚤感染或自发性皮炎（通常由毒藤、荨麻蜇伤或接触性过敏反应引起）引起的皮

肤瘙痒，并有助于缓解疼痛，同时减少轻微烧伤留下的疤痕。冲洗液还会给您的宠物带来令人愉悦的气

味。

In large animals, bee balm tea can be used as a douche or enema to treat fungal or bacterial infections, or to treat

irritations of the rectum or vagina.

对于大型动物，蜂香茶可用作冲洗剂或灌肠剂，以治疗真菌或细菌感染，或治疗直肠或阴道的刺激。

A dilute infusion can be used as a gentle antiseptic and anti-inflammatory eyewash or ear wash, especially if a

fungal or bacterial infection is suspected. For application in the eye, don’t make the infusion too strong—it should

be only light yellow in color. Rinse the eye and surrounding tissues with the use of an irrigation syringe. To add

stronger antimicrobial activity to the rinse, a pinch of dried Oregon grape root or certified organic goldenseal can be

added to the infusion while it is steeping. Just remember to keep the eye rinse very weak. Ear rinses can be made

much stronger.

稀释输液可用作温和的防腐剂和抗炎洗眼剂或洗耳剂，特别是在怀疑真菌或细菌感染时。涂抹在眼睛上

时，输液不要太浓——它的颜色应该只是浅黄色。使用冲洗注射器冲洗眼睛和周围组织。为了在冲洗液中

添加更强的抗菌活性，可以在浸泡时将一小撮干燥的俄勒冈葡萄根或经过认证的有机金印添加到浸泡液

中。请记住，冲洗眼睛的力度要非常弱。洗耳的效果可以更强一些。

Bee balm works well for low-grade urinary tract infections, and you might find it useful for kidney infections as

well. Unless you can get your animal to drink the tea, a glycerin-based tincture is probably your best bet: administer

12–25 drops per 20 pounds of animal weight two to three times per day.

蜂膏对于低度尿路感染效果很好，您可能会发现它对于肾脏感染也很有用。除非你能让你的动物喝茶，

否则甘油酊剂可能是你最好的选择：每 20 磅体重的动物服用 12-25 滴，每天 2-3 次。

Availability: Wild harvested or organically grown bee balm is available through herb retailers, as is the tincture.

Seeds and plants can be purchased through specialty catalogs and nurseries.

可获得性：野生收获或有机种植的蜂香膏和酊剂均可通过药草零售商购买。种子和植物可以通过专业目录

=== PAGE 97 ===
和苗圃购买。

Propagation and Harvest: Bee balm reseeds readily and transplants well. This is an excellent plant to introduce

into your herb garden. No stratification or other special treatment is required, and the plant is adaptable to almost

any soil. Gather the upper parts of this plant when it is in full bloom (May through September, depending on

location), which is when the parts are the most potent. Pluck individual leaves to minimize impact, or gather the

stem and leaves after the plant has bloomed and gone to seed. If the latter is your choice, clip the stems about 1 inch

above ground level to allow for perennial regrowth and root protection. When gathering while the plant is in bloom,

always be sure to leave plenty of flowers intact for pollination and seed development.

繁殖和收获：蜂香膏很容易重新播种并且移植得很好。这是一种非常适合引入您的药草园的植物。不需要

分层或其他特殊处理，该植物几乎可以适应任何土壤。当这种植物盛开时（五月到九月，取决于地点）收

集该植物的上部部分，这是这些部分最有效的时候。摘下单片叶子以尽量减少影响，或在植物开花并结籽

后收集茎和叶子。如果您选择后者，请将茎剪至距地面约 1 英寸的位置，以实现常年再生和根部保护。在

植物开花时采集时，一定要保留大量完整的花朵，以便授粉和种子发育。

Alternatives and Adjuncts: Combines well with catnip, chamomile, or fennel for digestive upsets and gas. Works

well as an infusion with echinacea, couch grass, raspberry leaf, or goldenrod for urinary or kidney disorders. As a

skin rinse, bee balm serves as a good base infusion to which feverfew flowers can be added for control of fleas.

替代品和辅助品：与猫薄荷、洋甘菊或茴香完美搭配，缓解消化不良和胀气。与紫锥菊、茅草、覆盆子叶

或黄花一起输注，可有效治疗泌尿系统或肾脏疾病。作为皮肤冲洗剂，蜂香膏是一种很好的基础浸液，可

以在其中添加小白菊花来控制跳蚤。

Cautions and Comments: Bee balm is a safe herb, but it often grows in areas that are heavily grazed by livestock,

where the presence of neighboring weeds may have led to the introduction of herbicides. Always check or ask for

evidence of spraying before you harvest.

注意事项和评论：蜂香膏是一种安全的药草，但它经常生长在牲畜大量放牧的地区，附近杂草的存在可能

导致使用除草剂。收获前务必检查或询问喷洒的证据。
